0d7bdfc71df876d6: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested 11 foreigners suspected of running an international online scam by posing as New York police officers in Bukit Ceylon on Tuesday.
The raid was conducted by Dang Wangi police at 5pm on Tuesday.
It followed information and intelligence gathered on a scam targeting victims in the United States.

Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those arrested were aged between 22 and 51 and comprised four South Africans, three Taiwanese, and one each from Mexico, Zimbabwe, Kenya and India.

"In the same operation, the raiding team seized three sets of New York Police Department (NYPD) uniforms, a New York police logo signboard and a map of New York City, which were used to deceive victims contacted through video calls.
"Also seized were 31 mobile phones, seven laptops, a monitor, a computer CPU and a router," he told a press conference today.
Azwan said digital forensic examinations and social media analysis of the seized devices indicated that the syndicate was suspected of carrying out scams by impersonating NYPD officers.

Investigations found that the suspects used artificial intelligence (AI) technology, including face-swapping techniques, background images and documents resembling official NYPD records, to convince victims that they were genuine police officers.
He said the syndicate used internet access to carry out online scams and was believed to have been operating since the middle of this year.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to deceive victims by claiming they were involved in criminal activities and money laundering.
"All those arrested have been remanded for four days, from Nov 25 to 28," he said.

ec36b65a3c23d86f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology.

The policy takes into account changes in the geopolitical landscape and increasingly complex traditional and non-traditional security threats, aiming to strengthen the country’s preparedness against emerging challenges.

Anwar said the policy adopts a Comprehensive Security approach, covering politics, the economy, society, the environment, public safety and technology, supported by collaboration between government agencies, the private sector, academia, non-governmental organisations and the public.
“Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed.
“We are no longer dealing solely with conventional forces or threats originating from other countries or within the region.

“This underscores the need to strengthen our cybersecurity capabilities, including investing in training and developing infrastructure to address new and increasingly unpredictable threats,” he said in his speech.

Anwar said security threats were no longer confined to conventional conflicts between countries, with cyberattacks increasingly targeting financial systems, defence networks and critical infrastructure.
“The National Security Policy takes into account the perspectives of previous policies, but I believe its strength lies in its ability to anticipate and address new issues and challenges,” he said.
He urged relevant ministries to consider setting up dedicated units to strengthen national capabilities, particularly in cybersecurity, while improving coordination between agencies.
He said these efforts must be supported by specialised expertise, including providing young officers with exposure and specialised training at leading institutions worldwide.
The National Security Policy 2026–2030 is a continuation of the previous 2021–2025 policy, which was based on the Comprehensive Security concept.

Under the latest policy, the previous nine National Security Core Values have been reorganised into 10 Strategic Focus Areas, including Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity, Sociopolitical Stability, National Cohesion, Effective Governance, Economic Resilience, Social Justice, Sustainable Development, People's Security, Security Diplomacy and Regional Cooperation, and Cybersecurity and Technology.
The last category is a new addition, reflecting the growing importance of cybersecurity and technological threats in national security planning.
The policy identifies 53 security issues, challenges and threats, which will be addressed through 30 strategies across the 10 focus areas.

Its implementation will be coordinated by the National Security Council under the Prime Minister’s Department, together with relevant ministries and agencies, with cooperation from the private sector and the public.

Monitoring mechanisms include National Security Council meetings, coordination and implementation monitoring committees, the National Security Index, security exercises and simulations, and integrated operations.

92d323bfccab9721: BANGKOK, Nov 26 — A huge explosion rocked an oil facility in Bangkok on Thursday, injuring nine people with three of them in a critical condition, Thai authorities said.
The blast was so strong that it rattled doors several kilometres away, according to AFP reporters, who saw a column of flames above the site followed by thick black smoke.
Thailand’s Energy minister Akanat Promphan, visiting the scene, said the blast sparked concern as the sprawling Phra Khanong site in eastern Bangkok was “also a residential area”.
But he told reporters it appeared the fire broke out at a distillation tower, “which was at least 100 metres (330 feet) away from the oil depot”, limiting the damage.
Thai energy conglomerate Bangchak Corporation, which runs the site, said it brought the situation under control within 30 minutes.
The cause of the incident was under investigation, it said in a statement.
The firm later said “air quality monitoring around the refinery shows normal levels”.
Akanat said authorities tested for carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and other contaminants in a one-kilometre (0.6-mile) radius around the facility and found no irregularities.
But the government was suspending production at the plant until the energy ministry was confident operations could resume without issue, he said.
Police told AFP that students from nearby schools had been evacuated, and residents were also asked to leave.
The Erawan Emergency Medical Centre, which is operated by Bangkok city authorities, reported nine people were injured -- three classified as critical, a change from its initial assessment.
Black smoke swept across the Thai capital’s skyline in the immediate aftermath of the blast.
A city-wide alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities urged people to avoid the area.
Bangchak Corporation’s website describes the site as a “modern complex refinery with a maximum capacity of 120,000 barrels per day”.
An explosion occurred at the refinery in July 2012, triggering a massive fire but no reported injuries. It was owned at the time by Bangchak Petroleum, which became the Bangchak Corporation.
The 2012 incident prompted questions about why such a large facility was located near a residential area.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said Thursday he was monitoring the situation, adding that it was too soon to apportion blame. — AFP

55fdee707b66a112: Microsoft has released an out-of-band hotpatch to fix a bug in November's Windows Server 2025 security update that could crash some servers when an IPv6 route expires.

The patch for the patch, KB5138318, addresses crashes on systems with Router Advertisement (RA) enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes. When a route timer expires, affected servers can halt with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE).
Issued on November 25, the corrective update takes effect without requiring a restart, according to Microsoft.

KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE means the kernel has detected corruption of a critical data structure and stopped the system. Microsoft has identified route-timer expiry as the trigger but hasn't explained the underlying coding fault.
Good to see the operating system being protected against the impact of the corruption. Less good for administrators wondering why their servers have suddenly misbehaved.

Lansweeper puts Windows Server 2025 at 7 percent of the servers it monitors, compared with 32 percent for Server 2022 and 33 percent for Server 2019. Only systems with the affected hotpatch and networking configuration are implicated.

Microsoft's Windows Server updates have not gone well over the last few months, with out-of-band updates issued in September, October, and November. An out-of-band update to deal with a problem introduced in a hotpatch (in this case, KB5131077) therefore carries with it a certain sense of inevitability.

Hotpatches are a way of getting OS security updates on a Windows Server without requiring a restart and so are, in theory, a boon for administrators keen on maximizing uptime. According to Microsoft, in addition to faster installations and better protection, there is "lower workload impact with less need to restart your machine."
Avoiding a planned restart is less of a selling point when the alternative is an unplanned crash. ®

c9d929f7e8b12eb6: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.
bc8875eabe52345f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former Damansara MP Tony Pua and incumbent Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong are under police investigation over their Facebook posts.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the two DAP politicians are being investigated separately, with Pua related to the declassification of documents relating to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon, Khoo on the closure of businesses in Kuala Terengganu during Friday prayers.

“Firm action without compromise will be taken against any party who deliberately makes or spreads statements that may cause public alarm,” he said in a statement this evening, adding that 55 reports had been filed over Pua’s post and two over Khoo’s remarks.
Both investigations are being handled by the Classified Criminal Investigation Unit under the Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) of the Criminal Investigation Department at Bukit Aman.
Pua’s case is being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for disclosing information, which carries a fine of up to RM1 million, up to one year’s jail, or both.

It is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities or services, which carries a fine of up to RM500,000, up to two years’ jail, or both.
Khoo’s case is being investigated under Section 298 of the Penal Code for deliberately intending to wound the religious feelings of any person, which carries up to one year’s jail, a fine, or both.

It is also being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code for statements that could cause public mischief by creating public fear or alarm, which carries up to two years’ jail, a fine, or both.
Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 has also been invoked in Khoo’s case.
Mohd Khalid said both cases were still at the investigation stage.
“The cases are still at the investigation stage, and police remind the public not to make speculation that could disrupt the investigation process,” he said.
He also urged all parties to steer clear of 3R, which stands for race, religion and royalty.
“Police also warn all parties not to ever touch on or raise 3R issues in any form that could jeopardise the peace and harmony of Malaysian society,” he said.
Pua posted on Facebook on November 18 what he said were declassified minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s September 18 meeting on Najib’s house arrest.
The pages reportedly recorded objections by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh to Najib serving the rest of his sentence under house arrest.

Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said demanded to know whether the minutes had been formally declassified, saying such a decision had to be made under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the document may have been declassified for court proceedings.

Khoo, who is also Melaka DAP chairman, questioned on November 20 a Kuala Terengganu City Council directive requiring businesses to close from 12.30pm to 2.30pm on Fridays, saying it affected non-Muslim traders.
He apologised the next day, and the Melaka government accepted the apology on November 23.

cb60572f0653af47: SINGAPORE, Nov 26 — Singapore has expressed disappointment over the proposed 20 per cent tariff on its exports to the United States (US), saying it disagrees with the findings of the United States Trade Representative (USTR).

“Singapore disagrees with the USTR’s findings and we are very disappointed with the proposed actions against Singapore,” the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) said in a statement on Thursday.

The USTR on Wednesday released a report on its findings and proposed actions against 14 economies, including Singapore and Malaysia, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 related to structural excess capacity and production in specific manufacturing sectors.
Urging the USTR to reconsider its proposed actions on Singapore, METI said it would continue to engage the USTR constructively, including exploring ways to reduce the tariff.
“We will be submitting further comments during the upcoming public consultation period to address the issues raised in the report,” it said.

METI noted that the USTR’s findings do not account for the structure of Singapore’s economy as its global trade surplus reflects an outward- and market-oriented economy as well as its status as a trusted business and trading hub.
“As a small country with limited resources, our priority is to ensure that our markets operate efficiently, and that Singapore remains competitive globally.

“Singapore’s economic policies do not protect our domestic market or subsidise manufacturing for export,” it said, adding that the republic's free trade agreements seek to lower barriers to trade and investment and are fully compliant with World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.

METI said that under the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (USSFTA), the US has enjoyed a consistent trade surplus with Singapore for over 20 years, with its overall trade surplus rising to US$33 billion (RM135.8 billion) in 2025 from US$27 billion in the previous year. — Bernama

db125f4552756b9b: <!--kg-card-end: html--> Grand Theft Auto VI is 2026’s breakout entertainment event. By the numbers, it made roughly $3.79 billion in revenue at launch, outpacing the lifetime earnings for megahit films like Avatar, The Odyssey, and Avengers: Infinity War. PlayStation called it their biggest launch of all time with over 39 million players on the platform alone. It’s the center of the current cultural zeitgeist, whether it’s because of the game’s controversy, music, love story, cultural legacy, or its accolades.

Entire households are playing GTA VI with one slight hitch: unlike movies, TV shows, or even books you can read side by side, a single-player, 40+ hour experience is tough to enjoy when you live together.

For some couples, the solution has been using more than one console or even multiple copies of the game. Married couple Meagan Kelley and Kyle Prahl typically switch between playing different games in the same room, or the same platforms in different parts of the house. The two are parents who find time to game after putting their son to bed. “The nice thing about having really young kids is they do go to bed super early,” Kelley told me. “Usually [my son] goes down and is asleep before eight, so then that's kind of like our prime gaming time.” The couple often plays different games in the same room, but for GTA VI “we're playing separately, so that kind of sucks because it's like we don't get a lot of time for each other,” Kelley said.

Although some men online have whined about Grand Theft Auto VI’s central romance, complaining about doing favors for their in-game girlfriend Lucia (“cuck simulator” being one common refrain), Kelley says the benefits to her real-life relationship are only positive. “It's funny that there's so much online discourse about GTA splitting up relationships and stuff when it's like something that can bring Kyle and I closer,” Kelley said. “Especially as we become parents and need to have more perspective on making sure that we're making time for ourselves.”

Dividing up time to play and sharing their experiences, she said, adds a new dimension to their mutual hobby. “When we are together taking care of our kid or having conversations, it's almost like book club,” Kelley said. “We share the different ways that we're experiencing the game with choices and stuff like that.”

Justin Massongill, another GTA VI player, and his wife recently had their second child. “She's taken on a lot,” he said. He bought the game for her, giving her priority to play so she could de-stress.

Massongill watched his wife play the first hour of the game; the next morning, he started his own. “We're kind of trying not to look too much at the other player's screen,” he said. “I don't want to, you know, get spoiled on things. But it's also such a massive game that what are the chances that we're going to see the same thing in the first place?”

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Madeline Blondeau and her fiancée decided to buy their copy of Grand Theft Auto VI together. The $80 price tag wasn’t so bad between the two of them; they downloaded the game, knowing that even with a PlayStation 5 and a PlayStation 5 Pro, they’d have to divvy up time between their single copy.

“We have been alternating our schedules,” Blondeau said. Her fiancée wakes up at 5 a.m. to start her IT job. Blondeau’s shift starts around 10 a.m. “We've sort of worked this out—me playing while she is working, and then her playing while I am finishing up my shift, trying to tiptoe around spoilers.”

Even as a queer couple, there’s an equality and care for each other in the experience Blondeau finds reassuring. “I think there's these very gendered expectations in relationships in terms of who games, who is the gamer of the household,” Blondeau said. You even see it in Grand Theft Auto, she adds, where Jason, the game’s male protagonist, will be the one with a controller in his hand. “Breaking down the gendered expectations of who is the gamer in the relationship really opens up a whole avenue for not getting into fights with your partner over video games,” Blondeau said.
“It feels like two people who figure their shit out, working out equitable time to experience something they've liked their whole lives, and talk about it.”

This past weekend, Blondeau’s fiancé left to grab groceries. She came back with something extra: the Grand Theft Auto trilogy for Nintendo Switch, a consolation prize for whoever wasn’t playing their shared copy of GTA VI. “I was in the mood to play Vice City,” her partner said. “We can trade off."

In Scotland, the Scottish National Party (SNP) posted GTA 6 memes so cringe that they talked about it on the floor of parliament. On November 19, the SNP social media accounts posted AI-generated pictures of Boris Johnson and Margaret Thatcher in the GTA style. “When the loading screen so long you start seeing characters you’ve never seen before,” one image said over a picture of Thatcher pouring a bag of “Scottish oil money” into the UK treasury.

Scotland’s Green Party didn’t find the memes funny. Rockstar is originally Scottish, was founded in Edinburgh, and still maintains a significant studio there. In parliament, Green co-leader Gillian Mackay said she was proud of what all of Rockstar’s workers had done to stand up against bad working conditions and produce a work of art like GTA 6. Then she made comments about SNP leader and Scottish First Minister John Swiney.

“Last night the SNP angered anti-AI campaigners by posting AI-generated GTA memes on its social media despite huge concerns about the impact of AI and AI data centers on artists, workers, and the environment,” Mackay said in the parliament session. “Does the first minister understand why people are concerned about his government’s approach to AI and the big companies behind it.”

The SNP deleted the memes and Swiney apologized. “First of all, let me say that I don’t want to offend anyone by anything that we get up to, so if I’ve offended anyone about that, I’m sorry about that. It was not my intention,” Swiney said in the Scottish parliament. Then he said he shared concerns about AI but defended the technology’s use for healthcare.

There will be more bad posts like this. Grand Theft Auto VI hasn’t been out for even a week and the memetic landscape around it will shift and change. We don’t even know what the dominant memes for the game are yet, let alone the innovative ways posters will iterate on them. Rest assured, however, that the governments of the world are watching and waiting to post their own variations and make it all cringe.

e4e7613e7956273e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today emphasised the importance of diplomacy in addressing regional security challenges, stressing the need to maintain strong ties with neighbouring countries.

Speaking at the launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 today, Anwar said Malaysia must prioritise diplomacy and maintain good relations with its neighbours to address regional security challenges while ensuring its own defence capabilities remain strong.

This includes maintaining diplomatic engagement with Myanmar to address longstanding issues surrounding the repatriation of refugees from Myanmar in Malaysia, as well as pushing, through Asean, for a Code of Conduct on the South China Sea.
“When my fellow ministers discuss whether we should maintain good relations with Myanmar’s government, my answer is yes.
“Why? Because it is necessary to resolve many of the problems we are facing.

“The issue involving 200,000 Myanmar nationals in Malaysia cannot be resolved by international organisations or foreign countries, regardless of how extensively they discuss the matter. We have to resolve it ourselves,” Anwar said.
Anwar said Malaysia is also seeking assurances from Myanmar that the safety of those being repatriated would be guaranteed and that their situation could be monitored upon their return.

He stressed that the government was not sending them back to face harm, adding that failing to address the issue would place a greater financial burden on Malaysia and potentially worsen public frustration and security concerns.
Malaysia has faced international criticism over its approach to the refugee issue involving Myanmar.
“Sometimes, refugees are unable to find employment, and this can contribute to an increase in crime-related issues, for example.
“That is why, in my view, discussions on national security must also take into account the wisdom of maintaining good diplomatic relations with neighbouring and regional countries,” Anwar said.

On the South China Sea dispute, Anwar stressed that Malaysia would continue to pursue diplomatic negotiations with China through Asean while strengthening its defence capabilities to safeguard the country’s maritime interests and sovereignty.

He said that Malaysia would continue working with Asean to pursue negotiations with China and push for the finalisation of a South China Sea Code of Conduct, which he said should be anchored in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982.
“I am not suggesting that Malaysia does not face problems.
“Malaysia is a maritime nation, and we have issues involving our neighbours and our maritime boundaries.
“However, the existence of these issues does not mean we are enemies or that they should lead to tensions in our bilateral relations,” Anwar said.
He added that Chinese Premier Li Qiang had also agreed to step up efforts towards finalising the Code of Conduct during the recent Asean meeting.
Asean and China missed their 2026 target for concluding the code but have reaffirmed their commitment to expedite the talks, with no new deadline set.
“Our Navy must always be prepared. We have consistently reminded them that defence is a major responsibility, and they must remain vigilant and maintain control over our waters.
“But we have not experienced the kind of confrontations seen in the Philippines, nor have we been involved in similar incidents.

“I have chosen the diplomatic path, although I agree with the calls made by the defence minister and the Defence Ministry for us to strengthen our capabilities and readiness to safeguard our national interests,” Anwar said.

The launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 was also attended by Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and National Security Council director-general Datuk Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin.
d2f54b6fea97893e: PETALING JAYA: Malaysian hotels are urging the government to reconsider plans to introduce a new visa requirement for Indian nationals – set to take effect on Jan 1 – saying the policy could impact tourist arrivals from the “strategic” market.
In a statement, the Malaysian Association of Hotels (MAH) said the country welcomed some 1.57 million tourists from India in 2025, a 14.6% increase from the 1.36 million recorded in 2024.
In the first half of 2026 alone, 738,000 tourists from India visited the country.
MAH president Christina Toh said Indian visitors bring business from individual travellers, families, tour groups, religious travel, weddings and corporate events.
However, an extra step in planning a trip may lead Indian travellers to choose destinations with easier entry, she cautioned.
On Nov 17, the immigration department said Indian passport holders would need a valid visa to enter Malaysia from Jan 1, 2027, with applications opening through the MyVISA portal on Dec 1.

The requirement comes almost a month after the Indian high commission in Kuala Lumpur warned of a noticeable increase in Indians abusing the visa-free facility to seek employment, with many allegedly misled by agents offering false job promises.
The 30-day visa exemption was introduced in December 2023 as part of Malaysia's visa liberalisation plan to attract more foreign visitors and facilitate tourism, business and social visits.

Toh said weaker demand could affect occupancy, profitability and 2027 business budgets, while advance reservations, contracted group bookings, travel trade agreements and marketing investments could also be disrupted.

The wider economy could also feel the impact through lower tourism receipts and foreign exchange earnings, she said, adding that jobs and business for small and medium enterprises, including travel agencies, may be affected.
“The decision (to introduce a new visa requirement) should not be assessed from an immigration perspective alone.
“Its possible effects on the economy, employment, investment, and Malaysia’s international competitiveness also deserve careful study.”

Toh said as hotels have a direct stake in how easily visitors can plan their stay in Malaysia, the association hopes the government will consider a solution that deals firmly with abuse of visa, without adding a hurdle for genuine travellers.
She urged the government to extend the 30-day visa exemption until December 2027.
991f3824a0c8625f: PETALING JAYA: Beberapa Adun Negeri Sembilan akan mengangkat sumpah jawatan sebagai ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco), menurut jemputan kepada media dihantar pihak istana petang ini.
Menurut jemputan itu, istiadat berkenaan akan bermula pada 9 pagi esok di Istana Besar Seri Menanti.
Tiada butiran lanjut didedahkan namun jemputan itu memberi bayangan Adun Juasseh, Ismail Lasim, akan kekal sebagai menteri besar Negeri Sembilan.

Jemputan itu dihantar selepas Ismail dan Pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN) Zahid Hamidi secara berasingan menghadap Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir di Istana Hinggap, Seremban, hari ini.
Zahid turut diiringi Timbalan Pengerusi BN Mohamad Hasan dan Setiausaha Agung Umno Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.

Kedudukan Ismail menjadi tanda tanya selepas BN mengumumkan beliau meletak jawatan sebagai menteri besar minggu lalu. Bagaimanapun, Ismail kemudian menafikan mengemukakan peletakan jawatannya kepada pihak istana.
Pentadbiran Ismail beroperasi tanpa exco sejak Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan kesemua 10 ahli exco pada 20 Sept lalu.

Kesemua 10 Adun daripada BN dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) itu kemudian mencabar pelucutan jawatan mereka di mahkamah, namun akhirnya memutuskan untuk menarik balik saman berkenaan susulan dakwaan Ismail meletak jawatan sebagai menteri besar.
Meskipun Mahkamah Tinggi Seremban menegaskan peletakan jawatan Ismail belum disahkan, 10 bekas exco itu tetap meneruskan penarikan balik saman berkenaan.

Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan mereka selepas kesemua exco itu menegaskan bahawa tindakan menyingkirkan baginda pada April lalu adalah sah dan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar merupakan pemerintah baharu negeri itu.
Pihak istana berpandangan tindakan mereka bercanggah dengan sumpah taat setia kepada pemerintah dan institusi diraja.
d0c77fbef346c7fb: PETALING JAYA: Polis berjaya menumpaskan satu sindiket penipuan dalam talian yang menyamar sebagai pegawai Jabatan Polis New York (NYPD) yang menyasarkan warga di Amerika Syarikat (AS) sebagai mangsa mereka.
Ketua Polis Dang Wangi, Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin berkata aktiviti sindiket itu terbongkar dalam satu serbuan di sebuah unit kediaman di Bukit Ceylon, Kuala Lumpur, pada Selasa, lapor Harian Metro.

Katanya, dalam serbuan itu polis menahan 11 warga asing terdiri daripada empat warga Afrika Selatan, tiga warga Taiwan serta masing-masing seorang warga Mexico, Zimbabwe, Kenya dan India, berusia antara 22 hingga 51 tahun.

"Pasukan serbuan turut merampas tiga pasang pakaian seragam 'New York Police Department', papan logo Polis New York dan peta Bandar Raya New York, digunakan bagi mengaburi mangsa yang dihubungi menerusi panggilan video.
"Turut dirampas 31 unit telefon bimbit, tujuh unit komputer riba, satu unit monitor, satu unit CPU dan satu unit router ," katanya.

Azwan berkata, hasil pemeriksaan forensik digital dan analisis media sosial terhadap peranti dirampas, mendapati sindiket berkenaan disyaki terbabit dalam kegiatan penipuan dengan menyamar sebagai anggota polis NYPD.

Katanya, suspek menggunakan teknologi kecerdasan buatan (AI) menerusi teknik 'Face Swap' atau pertukaran wajah dan imej latar belakang serta dokumen menyerupai dokumen rasmi NYPD bagi menyakinkan mangsa.

"Modus operandi sindiket berkenaan adalah memperdaya mangsa dengan mendakwa mereka terbabit dalam kegiatan jenayah serta pengubahan wang haram," katanya yang menambah sindiket itu dipercayai beroperasi sejak pertengahan tahun ini.
Ahmad Azwan berkata semua individu ditahan direman selama empat hari bermula 25 hingga 28 Nov ini bagi membantu siasatan mengikut Seksyen 420 dan 511 Kanun Keseksaan.
29e4cb22f7979c7b: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A man who died after trying to stop cable thieves in Johor has sparked public outrage, with calls for tougher penalties against those responsible for the increasingly disruptive crime.
S. Thanus, 22, was run over on Tuesday while trying to stop suspected cable thieves in Taman Nusa Bestari and succumbed to his injuries on Thursday.
Johor MIC chairman K. Raven Kumar expressed condolences to Thanus's family and called on the public to alert police rather than put their lives at risk by confronting suspected cable thieves.
The authorities must track down those responsible, he said.
Malaysian Public Transport Users Association president Ajit Singh Johl said cable theft should be treated as a threat to national interests rather than merely an ordinary theft offence.
He said the crime was not just about the monetary value of stolen cables but also the disruption to essential services and hardship caused to commuters.
A significant proportion of cable theft cases involved railway infrastructure, including MRT and LRT lines, where damaged cables could disrupt public transport operations, he said.
"Cable theft should not be treated as ordinary theft. It should be treated as treason because the damage goes far beyond the value of the cables stolen.
"The crime is not just against the utility provider but against millions of consumers and public transport users who suffer when services are disrupted," he said.
Ajit Singh said penalties for cable theft needed to be reviewed through legislative amendments, warning that the crime would continue if punishments did not reflect the extent of the damage caused.
"Until the punishment for cable theft is reviewed, this will keep happening. We need to take it much more seriously than standard theft because of the wider consequences," he said.

Cable theft along rail tracks has been on the rise, with Prasarana Malaysia Bhd recording 72 cases last year, up 68 per cent from 42 in 2024. The thefts caused RM20.6 million in losses over three years and disrupted rail services.
e157b272c13d062f: PETALING JAYA: Several Negeri Sembilan assemblymen will take their oath of office as state executive council members, according to a media invitation sent by the palace this evening.
The invitation states that the ceremony will start at 9am at Istana Besar Seri Menanti tomorrow.
No further details were disclosed, but it hints that Juasseh assemblyman Ismail Lasim will remain as Negeri Sembilan menteri besar.
FMT has reached out to Ismail for comment.
The invitation was sent after Ismail and Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi met Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir separately at Istana Hinggap in Seremban today.
Zahid was joined by BN deputy chairman Mohamad Hasan and Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
There was uncertainty over the status of Ismail's position after BN announced that he had resigned as menteri besar last week. However, he later denied submitting his resignation to the palace.
Ismail's administration has been without exco members ever since Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all 10 of them on Sept 20.

The 10 assemblymen from BN and Perikatan Nasional later went to the courts to challenge their sackings, but eventually decided to withdraw the suit following Ismail's alleged resignation as menteri besar.
While the Seremban High Court pointed out that Ismail’s resignation had not yet been confirmed, the 10 former exco members proceeded with the withdrawal of the suit.
Tuanku Muhriz had revoked their appointments following their assertion that his purported removal in April was legitimate and that Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar was the new ruler.
The palace viewed their actions as inconsistent with their oath of loyalty to the ruler and the royal institution.

d0bc4ea904511dad: The UK government is working "around the clock" on contingency plans for Capita contracts after the outsourcer's CEO quit and its shares plunged, a Cabinet Office minister told MPs.

Capita announced plans this week to raise around £190 million through a share issue in the first half of 2027 after warning of sharply lower profits and further costs linked to its Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract.
The outsourcer "should be absolutely ashamed of its performance" on the £239 million contract, Sally Jameson, parliamentary secretary in the Cabinet Office, told MPs on Tuesday.
"We have seen evidence that it has stepped up in recent months and begun to rectify the problem, but it is inexcusable that it let the situation get to this point," she said.
Adolfo Hernandez stepped down as CEO with immediate effect on Monday, with finance chief Pablo Andres taking over. Shares fell around 70 percent following the announcement.
In the House of Commons, Jameson was asked about the government's plans if Capita were unable to carry out the remainder of its contract given the outsourcer's performance on the CSPS.

"On contingency planning, it is important that we stabilize the situation and that Capita can continue to deliver the pension scheme. However, the government is working across departments, as we do in relation to all strategic suppliers, to ensure that the relevant contingency plans are in place. People are working around the clock on that," she said.
Jameson said contingency planning for the pension scheme was already underway before Monday's announcement, describing it as standard practice for major government suppliers.
She told the Chamber that the Cabinet Office was "currently arranging to meet the new CEO in the coming days" following Hernandez's departure.

The Register first exposed problems with Capita's CSPS portal last December. The site, serving 1.5 million current and former public servants, rejected login details even for newly created accounts, contained broken and circular links, and displayed dummy text.

In January this year, the Cabinet Office was forced to promise "interim support measures" for the CSPS following Capita's botched takeover, including 150 additional government staff to clear the backlog in cases.

Speaking in Parliament, Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the Public Accounts Committee, said there had been "some tragic and dreadful cases" since Capita took over administration last December.

"I heard of one poor lady who was living on benefits because she could not get the bereavement payments she needed after her sister's death. I have heard of a member of parliamentary staff, not far from this Chamber, who is having to delay his retirement by a year because he cannot even get a statement from the scheme."

The government has withheld nearly £10 million in contractual payments over Capita's performance. It is currently locked in negotiations over further penalties following the appointment of an auditor, first revealed in July. At the time, Hernandez apologized for Capita's performance but refused to commit to further compensation.
The National Audit Office and Public Accounts Committee have both launched probes into Capita's handling of the CSPS and its appointment as a contractor.

In February, The Register revealed a legal challenge to the government's award of the separate Synergy shared services contract to Capita. The deal covers HR and finance services across four Whitehall departments and associated arm's-length bodies. Rival bidder Sopra Steria, which owns incumbent provider SSCL, alleges Capita's bid was abnormally low and its proposed staffing raised concerns about delivery. Capita and the Department for Work and Pensions, which led the procurement, deny the allegations and say the competition was fair and open. Capita values the contract at £370 million.
The Public and Commercial Services Union is now calling on the government to scrap Capita's shared services contract with the DWP, citing the outsourcer's troubled handling of CSPS. ®
4ebfdacb29f33701: KUCHING: Non-Sarawakian DAP ministers and deputy ministers will not campaign in the 13th Sarawak state election, with the state chapter taking charge of its own campaign, said Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen.
He said the decision was made in the spirit of the Madani government and out of respect for the party's coalition partners at federal level.

"Sarawak DAP will lead the campaign on the ground, with our own leaders, our own members and our own message. Our record and our commitment to the people of Sarawak will speak for themselves," he said in a statement.

Chong said the decision was part of a consensus reached following his meeting with DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke in Kuala Lumpur today, after Parti Keadilan Rakyat's (PKR) withdrawal from the state election.
In the spirit of democracy, he said Sarawak DAP maintained its position to contest in the upcoming state election.
"This isn't a new concession. It is a principle Sarawak DAP has always upheld. Matters concerning Sarawak are decided by Sarawak DAP solely.

"That has always included the number of seats we contest, the choice of candidates, and the signing of the watikah to contest under the DAP logo. These decisions are made here in Sarawak, by Sarawak DAP," he said.
Chong said the DAP Central Executive Committee had also reaffirmed its full respect for Sarawak DAP's autonomy and would abide by the arrangement.
DAP has so far confirmed that it will contest 12 seats in the state election.

Meanwhile, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has named candidates for all 82 seats, Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS) 26, Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) 12 and Parti Aspirasi Rakyat Sarawak (Aspirasi) one, while Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) has announced its intention to contest three seats.
The Election Commission has fixed Nov 28 for nomination day, followed by early voting on Dec 8 and polling on Dec 12.
073aa0425b4f875e: GEORGE TOWN: Kampung Makam was hit by flash floods following a heavy afternoon downpour today, with nearby Kampung Dodol also reportedly affected.
The rain, which began in the late afternoon, caused water levels to rise rapidly, inundating low-lying areas.
A resident took to TikTok Live to share footage of the situation in Kampung Makam, showing floodwaters reaching an adult's calf level at the compound.
He said about 20 houses were located in the village and told viewers he was moving his car to higher ground.
"It did not rain for long but our surroundings have been flooded. This is possibly worsened by the high tide phenomenon," he said.
In the comments section, a resident of nearby Kampung Dodol also reported similar flooding.
Rain was also reported in several parts of the mainland.
No evacuations had been reported so far, while local authorities and emergency personnel were monitoring the situation.
Penang residents have been advised to remain alert for thunderstorms and king tides expected to affect the state until tomorrow.
State Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said residents should remain vigilant during the ongoing northeast monsoon, particularly those living in low-lying and coastal areas.
b5cf4135eb16ab65: MOSCOW: Russian oil major Lukoil's withdrawal from international markets was driven by politics rather than the company's own choice, co-founder Vagit Alekperov said on Thursday in his first public comments on the planned sale of its overseas assets.
Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer, announced the sale of its international portfolio last year after the US imposed sanctions on the company in October 2025 over Russia's war in Ukraine.
Russia's largest oil producer, Rosneft, has not put its foreign assets up for sale.
The state-controlled company, which is also subject to US sanctions, is headed by Igor Sechin, a long-standing ally of president Vladimir Putin.
Germany placed Rosneft's local units under trusteeship in 2022 after the war upended Berlin's decades-long energy ties with Russia.
Lukoil's international asset sale is the most consequential action so far by a Russian company in the wake of Western sanctions over the Ukraine war, which started in February 2022.
"Lukoil did not make the decision to withdraw from international markets on its own. This was driven more by political factors," Alekperov told Russian state TV programme Vesti.
"However, we are not shutting the curtain completely. We still hope to return," he said.
Alekperov was Lukoil's CEO for nearly 30 years before he stepped down in April 2022 after some Western countries introduced sanctions against him.
US billionaire Todd Boehly said on Wednesday he had signed a deal with Lukoil for a consortium that includes the US International Development Finance Corp (DFC) to acquire the international assets.

Lukoil's overseas portfolio, which spans about 40 countries and includes oilfields in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and 9 other countries producing about 350,000 barrels of oil per day, is valued at around US$16 billion, two people familiar with the terms of the deal said.
cbaee9cb9f272f6f: PETALING JAYA: Three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) pilots and three civilians will be charged tomorrow for trafficking drugs using military assets.

Bukit Aman narcotics crime investigation department (NCID) director Hussein Omar Khan said the Attorney-General's Chambers had ordered the six to be charged under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 at the Shah Alam magistrates' court.

He said in a statement, action would also be taken against another seven suspects arrested for their alleged involvement in a drug smuggling syndicate under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.

Hussein said all 13 suspects, seven of whom were RMAF personnel, were arrested during a police operation from Nov 17 to 19, which also saw the seizure of 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million.

Home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said earlier today that the syndicate had used a military aircraft on 21 occasions to smuggle methamphetamine worth an estimated RM156 million before it was busted last week.

He said the syndicate’s cell in Tawau had used military assets seven times to smuggle 1.8 tonnes of methamphetamine, while its cell in Labuan had used military assets 14 times to smuggle 1.2 tonnes of drugs.
a0f024d3bfdec34f: PETALING JAYA: Polis membuka dua kertas berasingan berhubung hantaran Facebook oleh bekas Ahli Parlimen Petaling Jaya Utara Tony Pua dan Ahli Parlimen Kota Melaka Khoo Poay Tiong.

Menurut kenyataan, siasatan terhadap Pua berhubung hantaran mengandungi maklumat penyahklasfikasi dokumen pengampunan Najib Razak, manakala siasatan terhadap Khoo berhubung hantaran mengenai arahan penutupan premis perniagaan di Kuala Terengganu ketika solat Jumaat oleh Majlis Bandaraya Kuala Terengganu.

Siasatan terhadap Pua dijalankan bawah Seksyen 203A Kanun Keseksaan (KK) iaitu mendedahkan maklumat, dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia iaitu penggunaan tidak wajar kemudahan rangkaian atau perkhidmatan rangkaian.

Kes melibatkan Khoo pula disiasat bawah Seksyen 298 KK iaitu sengaja berniat hendak melukakan perasan agama mana-mana orang, Seksyen 505(b) KK iaitu kenyataan yang mendatangkan khianat awam dengan niat hendak menyebabkan atau mungkin menyebabkan ketakutan atau kegentaran awam, dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia.
Siasatan terhadap dua pemimpin DAP itu dikendalikan oleh Unit Siasatan Jenayah Terkelas Bukit Aman.
"Kes masih di peringkat siasatan dan polis mengingatkan orang ramai agar tidak membuat spekulasi yang boleh mengganggu proses siasatan," kata Ketua Polis Negara Khalid Ismail.

Polis turut memberi amaran kepada semua pihak agar tidak sesekali menyentuh atau membangkitkan isu 3R (kaum, agama, dan institusi diraja) dalam apa jua bentuk yang boleh menjejaskan keamanan dan keharmonian masyarakat.
"Tindakan tegas tanpa kompromi akan diambil terhadap mana-mana pihak yang dengan sengaja membuat atau menyebarkan kenyataan yang mungkin menimbulkan kegentaran awam," katanya.
Polis berkata kertas siasatan dibuka selepas menerima laporan berhubung hantaran Facebook oleh Pua dan Khoo.
Polis menerima sebanyak 55 laporan berhubung hantaran Pua, dan dua laporan berhubung kenyataan Khoo.
e581f3fcd790ea63: PETALING JAYA: Federal police are investigating DAP’s Tony Pua over his sharing of the declassified pardons board minutes on Najib Razak’s house arrest, as well as Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong over a controversial Facebook post.
Inspector-General of Police Khalid Ismail said 55 police reports had been lodged against Pua over his posting of the minutes on Facebook.

Two police reports were filed against Khoo over his Facebook post criticising the mandatory temporary closure of business premises during Friday prayers in Terengganu. The Melaka DAP chief has since apologised for the post.
“Both investigations are being handled by Bukit Aman’s classified crimes unit,” Khalid said in a statement.

Khalid said the 55 reports against Pua were being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for unauthorised disclosure of information obtained in the course of official duties, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (CMA) for improper use of network facilities.

The two reports against Khoo were being investigated under Section 298 of the Penal Code for wounding religious feelings, Section 505(b) for making statements conducive to public mischief, and Section 233 of the CMA.
“The cases are still being investigated, and the public are reminded not to make speculations that could interfere with the process,” he said.
Last week, Pua published on Facebook the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board's (FTPB) meeting concerning former prime minister Najib's conditional pardon.

He received flak over the post from several quarters, especially Umno leaders. However, Pua defended himself, saying he did not declassify the document and was not involved in the FTPB's decision-making process.

Khoo apologised for his post after being reprimanded by his Pakatan Harapan peers, notably Melaka PKR acting chief Adam Adli, who advised him to respect the laws of the respective states and religious sensitivities in such matters.

7c6dfc04823f8d83: LONDON: More details about Patrick Stewart's death have come to light.

Less than a month after the X-Men actor died at the age of 86, his official causes of death were determined to be Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to his death certificate obtained by TMZ.
The document also listed cardiopulmonary arrest – commonly known as cardiac arrest – as an immediate factor.
According to Alzheimers.gov, Lewy body dementia is "a brain disorder that can lead to problems with thinking, movement, behaviour, and mood."
The Star Trek: The Next Generation star's death certificate also revealed that his remains underwent alkaline hydrolysis, or water cremation.
The Cremation Association of North America explains that the process "uses water, alkaline chemicals, heat, and sometimes pressure and agitation, to accelerate natural decomposition."
It leaves behind a liquid that can be safely disposed of, alongside bone fragments that are dried and pulverised into a powder.
A day after his death on Oct 28, Stewart's family shared that he had died at his Los Angeles home "in the loving care of his wife", Sunny Ozell.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the Oct 29 post on Stewart's Instagram read.
"We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.
"He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role," the statement continued, "in his art and life."
In the weeks following his death, Ozell – whom Stewart married in 2013 – shared her own moving tribute to her late husband.
Writing on Instagram on Nov 11, she said: "We left nothing unsaid. He knew I loved him, and I know he loved me."
"We shared nearly two decades together, and we filled those years with so much living," the 47-year-old added.
"I've been overwhelmed by the public response to Patrick's death, and while I'm not at all surprised that he touched so many, I'm sincerely moved by the outpouring of sadness and loss."
008a2347b0f83ffc: KUALA LUMPUR: Muslims in Malaysia must set an example by embracing knowledge, upholding justice and having the courage to speak out against corruption and misconduct, even when the perpetrators hide behind the name of religion.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said young people must also have the courage to ask questions and examine the basis of every argument before accepting it.

"During the Dialog Negara, I was asked about religious controversies that divide society and how the people could distinguish between religious enlightenment and political views presented as though they were religious rulings.

"I stressed that knowledge is the foremost prerequisite for Islamic preaching. I knew Sheikh Yusuf al-Qaradawi as a teacher of profound knowledge, and I never heard him pass judgement on others arbitrarily," he said in a Facebook post.

Anwar said such an attitude should be emulated, particularly when some quarters readily issued fatwas without scriptural evidence to legitimise their political agendas, even in support of detrimental practices.

Last night, Anwar addressed various questions concerning government policies, considerations and decisions on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, which was also simulcast on RTMKlik, Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
09733edf054a3e70: TOKYO: Japan and China accused each other's ships on Thursday of intruding into waters near disputed islands that each claims as their territory and have caused diplomatic tensions for decades.
The incident occurred near uninhabited islands claimed as the Senkaku in Japan and the Diaoyu in China, which sit between Taiwan and Okinawa.
Japan's coast guard said that it had repeatedly warned two Chinese ships to leave the area after the vessels approached a Japanese fishing boat.
The two Chinese vessels entered the area at around 7.42am Thursday and were "trying to approach a Japanese fishing boat", Japan's coast guard said in a statement.

"Such activities by Chinese coast guard vessels constitute a violation of international law, and our patrol vessels are repeatedly issuing demands for the vessels to leave Japan's territorial sea," it said.
The Japanese coast guard told AFP that this is the fifth time this year a Chinese vessel had approached a Japanese fishing boat in the area.
The Chinese government reiterated its claim over the islands and accused Japan of violating its sovereignty.
"China has already lodged serious representations with Japan," Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said.
"Chinese coast guard vessels took necessary control measures against the relevant vessels in accordance with the law," he said.

The latest incident comes after ships from Japan's and China's coast guards faced off near disputed islands in July, with each side claiming they drove out the other's vessels that had intruded into their territorial waters.
Relations between Tokyo and Beijing are at historic lows after prime minister Sanae Takaichi suggested last year that Japan could intervene militarily in the event that China attacked Taiwan.
A furious China, which views the democratic island as part of its territory, retaliated with trade restrictions and warned its citizens not to travel to Japan.
Chinese president Xi Jinping snubbed Takaichi at a regional meeting in Shenzhen last week, which marked the Japanese premier's first trip to China since she took office.

6ab1e618c85f14ee: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd's net profit fell 8.2 per cent to RM609.54 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) from RM664.33 million a year earlier.
Revenue rose 16 per cent to RM1.13 billion from RM968.7 million, driven by stronger contributions from its property investment and hospitality and leisure segments.

Excluding exceptional items, IOI Properties' underlying earnings improved by 25 per cent, supported by contributions from South Beach office tower and JW Marriott in Singapore, as well as improved occupancy at IOI Central Boulevard Towers.
Hospitality and leisure was among the strongest performers, with operating profit increasing more than sixfold.
This wss supported by higher hotel occupancy and average room rates in Malaysia and Singapore.
In Malaysia, W Kuala Lumpur and Le Meridien Putrajaya recorded occupancy rates of 87 per cent each, while Moxy Putrajaya achieved 82 per cent.

Group chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said the performance reflected the group's strategy to diversify its income streams and strengthen recurring earnings across its three core business segments.
The property development segment recorded sales of RM454.2 million during the quarter, with Malaysia contributing RM388.3 million, or 86 per cent, of the total.
The group's unbilled sales stood at RM2.46 billion, providing earnings visibility over the near to medium term.
The proposed sale of industrial land at IOI Industrial Park Banting to Bridge Data Centres is on track for completion by the fourth quarter of calendar year 2026.
Meanwhile, the property investment segment benefited from resilient rental demand at its retail malls and offices, including IOI City Mall and IOI Mall Puchong.
The group's acquisition of Asia Square Tower 2 in Singapore, completed on Sept 17, adds 2.58 million sq ft of net lettable office space to its portfolio.
Separately, the listing of IOIPG Reit on Nov 25 raised about RM2 billion, strengthening the group's balance sheet and supporting its capital recycling initiatives.
Lee said the group remained positive about its outlook for the rest of FY27, underpinned by its diversified property portfolio, healthy unbilled sales and growing recurring income.
1dc215371c6dda76: KUALA LUMPUR: Lagenda Properties Bhd's net profit rose 38.8 per cent to RM62 million in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM44.7 million a year earlier, on the back of higher revenue.
Revenue surged 58.7 per cent to RM404.5 million from RM254.9 million, while pre-tax profit increased 54.5 per cent to RM95.3 million from RM61.7 million.
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased 32.3 per cent to RM1 billion from RM758.2 million, while net profit grew 21 per cent to RM162.7 million from RM134.5 million.
The property development segment remained the group's largest revenue contributor, recording RM359.9 million in revenue for the third quarter, up 56.7 per cent from a year earlier.
Lagenda also recorded its highest-ever quarterly confirmed sales of RM573.5 million, bringing confirmed sales for the nine-month period to RM1.45 billion.
As of September this year, its unbilled sales stood at a record RM1.93 billion, while bookings amounted to RM480.7 million, providing visibility for future revenue.
The company had an unlaunched landbank of 1,559.5 hectares, with an estimated remaining gross development value of RM9.5 billion.

Lagenda said it would focus on construction progress and upcoming launches across its existing townships in Johor, Kedah, Negri Sembilan and Pahang, while maintaining a disciplined approach to landbanking, project execution and cost management.
12d230263f4e750e: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's gender gap narrowed slightly in 2025, with the Malaysia Gender Gap Index (MGGI) rising to 0.711 from 0.708 the previous year, driven mainly by improvements in women's economic participation and opportunities.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said the economic participation and opportunity subindex increased to 0.728 from 0.703 in 2024.
Women's labour force participation rate edged up to 56.6 per cent from 56.5 per cent, while their mean monthly salaries and wages rose to RM3,635 from RM3,499.

The number of women working as legislators, senior officials and managers also increased to 241,000 from 219,000, while those in professional and technical occupations rose to 1.8 million from 1.7 million.

"The MGGI measures the gender gap between women and men in four areas, namely economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment," DOSM said in its MGGI 2026 report released today.
A score of 1.000 indicates full equality between women and men.
DOSM said the educational attainment subindex stood at 1.064 in 2025, compared with 1.073 in 2024.

"Female students recorded higher gross enrolment rates at the secondary and tertiary levels, at 95.9 per cent and 57.1 per cent respectively, while the rate for both males and females at the primary level was 99.7 per cent," it said.
The health and survival subindex stood at 0.957 in 2025, with women's life expectancy at birth rising to 77.8 years from 65.6 years in 1970.
However, political empowerment remained the weakest area, with a score of just 0.094.
DOSM said women accounted for only 15.6 per cent of ministerial positions and 13.5 per cent of seats in the Dewan Rakyat.
"This reflects the continuing challenges in achieving gender balance in political leadership and decision-making in Malaysia," it said.
At the state level, Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest MGGI score at 0.781, followed by Labuan at 0.756 and Putrajaya at 0.754.
Five states recorded scores below the national level of 0.711, namely Melaka (0.707), Terengganu (0.706), Pahang (0.704), Sarawak (0.698) and Johor (0.693).

021d7193e8027ab4: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply Bill 2027 via a voice vote at its third reading, capping weeks of committee-stage debate.
This is Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth and biggest federal budget, although development spending is still lower than the record allocation announced for 2023, at RM97 billion.
Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Ramli Mohd Nor declared the Bill approved late this afternoon after the Ministry of Youth and Sports wrapped up the final round of debates.
No Opposition MPs rose to call for bloc voting.
As a voice vote does not record a head count, the outcome does not show how many MPs backed the Bill.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, was present in the House alongside some senior ministers.

The RM459.8 billion spending plan comes to RM510 billion when investments from government-linked investment companies, statutory bodies, Minister of Finance Incorporated companies and public-private partnerships are factored in.
It passes ahead of a potential general election that might be called next year.
Of the RM459.8 billion direct federal allocation, RM376.8 billion is earmarked for operating expenditure while RM83 billion goes toward development.
Today’s uncontested vote was largely telegraphed following a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) inked on October 29 between the Anwar administration and 13 MPs.

The CSA, announced the same day the Bill cleared its policy stage, was signed by six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, six former Bersatu MPs and Muda’s Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Under the pact, the signatories will back the budget and Anwar’s administration in return for the same constituency allocations as government backbenchers.
The agreement also covers institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and separating the powers of the attorney general and public prosecutor.
Anwar had previously confirmed that constituency allocations for the 13 signatories would be disbursed upon the Supply Bill’s final approval in Parliament.
5ae3ab70795c3649: KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd's net profit fell 29.3 per cent to RM118.9 million in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) from RM168.2 million a year earlier.
Revenue declined 11.8 per cent to RM1.07 billion from RM1.21 billion, while profit before tax (PBT) dropped 26.1 per cent to RM192.6 million from RM260.7 million.
However, the property developer's nine-month performance remained strong, with net profit rising 39.4 per cent year-on-year to RM599.7 million from RM430.2 million.
SD Property's pre-tax profit for the nine-month period increased 25.7 per cent to RM828.2 million from RM659.1 million, despite revenue easing 3.7 per cent to RM3.03 billion from RM3.15 billion.

The group attributed its stronger nine-month profitability to higher contributions from its investment and asset management (IAM) portfolio, which recorded a 63.8 per cent increase in revenue to RM221.6 million and more than doubled its pre-tax profit to RM213.6 million, supported by recurring income from data centre and retail assets.
The property development segment remained its largest contributor, recording revenue of RM2.7 billion and pre-tax profit of RM615.9 million.

Group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Azmir Merican said the record nine-month profitability reflected the growing contribution of recurring income assets alongside the group's township and industrial developments.
For the nine months, the group recorded RM3.7 billion in property launches and RM2.5 billion in sales. Unbilled sales stood at RM3.6 billion as at Sept 30, 2026.

The group also launched its maiden Melbourne development, Aurum, with an estimated gross development value of A$1.08 billion (RM3.2 billion), and secured shareholders' approval for a proposed land acquisition in Kulai, Johor, for a township with an estimated GDV of RM3 billion.
The group is also preparing for a potential industrial and logistics real estate investment trust (Reit) listing as it expands its assets under management, although it ruled out a listing in 2027.
President and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Azmir Merican said the group was working towards the Reit but had yet to determine its listing timeline or disclose the assets to be included.

He said the group would consider recycling its capital through a Reit once its asset portfolio had grown sufficiently and generated attractive yields, adding that it was still at an early stage of preparations.
"We do feel that as we build our assets under management and get to a point where the yields are attractive, it will be an appropriate time to recycle capital," he said.
He added that it was too early to speculate on whether the listing would take place in 2028.
For FY26, SD Property is targeting full-year launches of about RM5 billion and aims to grow its assets under management to more than RM10 billion by 2028.

157fc65fb2db8595: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia akan mengutamakan usaha mewujudkan sistem pengukuran, pelaporan dan pengesahan karbon sendiri sebelum menceburi perdagangan kredit karbon antarabangsa, sementara menunggu penggubalan Akta Perubahan Iklim Negara bagi memperuntukkan kawal selia yang lebih menyeluruh.

Menteri Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam Arthur Joseph Kurup berkata program Forest Carbon Offset (FCO) yang baru dilancarkan dan dilaksanakan di bawah Dana Hutan Malaysia (MFF) akan menyediakan asas teknikal bagi pembangunan pangkalan data kredit karbon negara.

Beliau berkata langkah mewujudkan kerangka kerja domestik yang kukuh amat penting bagi memastikan Malaysia mematuhi Artikel 6 Perjanjian Paris serta mekanisme antarabangsa seperti Mekanisme Pelarasan Sempadan Karbon (CBAM) Kesatuan Eropah dan Skim Pengimbangan serta Pengurangan Karbon bagi Penerbangan Antarabangsa (CORSIA).
“Penting bagi kita untuk mempunyai sistem pengesahan, pengukuran dan pelaporan sendiri.

“Apabila usaha ini dilaksanakan, kita akan dapat mewujudkan pangkalan data mengenai kredit karbon di negara ini, sekali gus membolehkan perdagangan antarabangsa dijalankan. Ini juga membolehkan kita mematuhi keperluan CBAM dan CORSIA, iaitu mekanisme pengimbangan karbon bagi sektor penerbangan antarabangsa,” katanya kepada pemberita selepas merasmikan program FCO di sini hari ini.

Mengenai program itu, Arthur berkata ia dibangunkan berasaskan Dasar Pasaran Karbon Kebangsaan yang dilancarkan awal tahun ini, yang menyediakan mekanisme berasaskan pasaran bagi mempelbagaikan sumber pembiayaan untuk pemuliharaan hutan, selain geran kerajaan dengan menarik pelaburan daripada sektor swasta.

“Paling penting selepas ini, bagi program karbon atau perhutanan ini, kita tidak mahu hanya bergantung pada geran kerajaan. Sebaliknya, melalui program FCO, kita berupaya menarik lebih banyak pelaburan daripada sektor swasta agar usaha ini dapat dilaksanakan menerusi pendekatan menyeluruh yang melibatkan keseluruhan kerajaan dan seluruh negara,” katanya.

Beliau berkata kementerian juga berhasrat memastikan semua kerajaan negeri mempunyai pendirian yang selaras dalam melaksanakan inisiatif tersebut, memandangkan hal ehwal tanah dan perhutanan terletak di bawah bidang kuasa negeri.

Mengenai usaha penyahkarbonan Malaysia, Arthur berkata negara ini berjaya mengekalkan purata pertumbuhan Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar (KDNK) sekitar lima peratus dalam tempoh 15 tahun lepas, di samping mengurangkan intensiti pelepasan karbon sebanyak 37 peratus setakat 2021.

“Malaysia boleh menjadi contoh kepada negara lain di seluruh dunia bahawa kita tidak perlu mengorbankan pertumbuhan ekonomi untuk pemuliharaan alam sekitar kerana kedua-duanya boleh dicapai secara seiring,” katanya.

Terdahulu, Arthur menyaksikan majlis pertukaran perjanjian kerjasama antara MFF dengan empat organisasi, iaitu Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Yinson Holdings Berhad, Pusat Kerjasama Alam Sekitar Luar Negara Jepun (OECC) dan FRIM Inc Sdn Bhd.

Kerjasama tersebut memberi tumpuan kepada penerokaan peluang dalam pembangunan projek karbon hutan, pemuliharaan biodiversiti, pemulihan ekosistem, perkongsian pengetahuan teknikal serta pembangunan kapasiti.
3e44a71fc7f63f38: More than eight years after Rodrigo Duterte announced the Philippines would withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), the country’s former president is about to begin his trial in The Hague. Duterte faces charges of crimes against humanity over alleged killings carried out during his deadly war on drugs. The trial, which begins on 30 November, comes at a precarious moment for the court, as the United States ramps up its efforts to undermine the institution. “Nothing has really quite approached this level of hostility we’re seeing coming from President Trump, or more particularly Marco Rubio,” explains Carrie McDougall, an associate professor at Melbourne Law School, speaking on The Conversation Weekly podcast. The US has never joined the ICC, citing concerns about politically motivated prosecutions of its nationals. But the court can investigate alleged war crimes committed by Americans on the territory of its member countries. McDougall says the US has “made no bones” about its opposition to the investigation of US nationals and the prosecution of Israeli nationals. In October, the Trump administration extended sanctions against individual ICC judges and prosecutors to the court as a whole. The sanctions threaten the court’s access to banking and IT services, as well as its ability to engage with victims and witnesses, McDougall says. The US has also been pressuring countries to withdraw from the court. McDougall attributes the decisions by Venezuela, Chad and Nauru to withdraw from the ICC to that pressure. Meanwhile, Duterte’s case illustrates both the powers and limitations of the court. “The reality is that the court itself doesn’t have any enforcement powers,” McDougall says. Instead, it relies on the Security Council – which has never used its enforcement powers to assist the court – and countries to cooperate with it. Duterte was arrested by his own country’s authorities. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu are both subject to ICC arrest warrants, but Russia and Israel have refused to cooperate in the arrest of their leaders. Neither country is a member of the ICC. While the ICC doesn’t have its own enforcement powers, arrest warrants still have some power; they can restrict leaders’ ability to travel overseas and potentially deter others from committing crimes. And, McDougall says: There is no statute of limitations, so those ICC arrest warrants can be enforced after individuals have lost power and lost the protection of their states. Duterte’s case also demonstrates that withdrawing from the ICC does not necessarily shield political leaders from prosecution, explains McDougall. Once a state … files a notice of withdrawal, it takes a year to become effective, and the ICC retains jurisdiction over any crimes committed up until that effective withdrawal date. So will the ICC survive? McDougall says the US sanctions “will impede the court’s ability to fulfil its mandate” and that the threat is “very serious.” She also warns that US attacks on international institutions risk emboldening other countries, including China and Russia, that want to reshape that order. “I think we are facing something of a crossroads,” she says. McDougall describes the ICC as the “canary in the coal mine” for the international legal order: It is required to hold to account those responsible for international crimes, particularly when we’re talking about the leaders of states. And so that puts a really big target on its back for would-be spoilers. Ultimately, though, McDougall does not expect a mass exodus from the ICC. I think a lot will actually hinge on how robustly other ICC states’ parties stand up for the court. 6bf0c41a82836e8a: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Sports Council (NSC) will revive the women's national e-sports team next year, with 12 athletes competing in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang and Honor of Kings, two mobile games featuring five-versus-five team battles.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari said the ministry was drawing up guidelines for e-sports with the Malaysian E-sports Federation, involving other ministries.
"We see that e-sports is no longer just a sport or merely a game. It is now a form of industry," he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the issue had been discussed at the Cabinet Committee on Sports Development, including how to steer e-sports in a more positive direction.
"Gaming can also lead to negative things, extremism and so on.
"That is why we are developing these clear guidelines, so that e-sports can be more positive and healthier," he said.
He said training facilities included the E-sports Integrated Hub in Puchong, Selangor, the national training centre at the National Sports Council in Bukit Jalil and 13 state-level e-sports studios.
He agreed that equipment at the facilities needed to be kept up to date.

He said e-sports had made history this year when Taj Izrin Aiman won a gold medal at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, describing it as the result of the National Sports Council's podium programme.
He added that RM500,000 had been allocated for the Malaysia Esports Accelerator Programme this year.
The ministry has been allocated RM1.213 billion for 2027, up about 2.5 per cent from RM1.183 billion this year.
b9e2cd8ef6fd4289: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A family has lost its young breadwinner after a 22-year-old man, who supported his bedridden mother and four siblings, died from injuries sustained in a hit-and-run involving suspected cable thieves.
S. Thanus died at Sultanah Aminah Hospital at 10am yesterday, after he was run over by a car driven by one of the suspects attempting to flee the scene in Taman Nusa Bestari here.

He remained unconscious since the incident, which occurred around 4.30am on Tuesday. His cause of death was determined to be a head injury consistent with injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
His death coincided with the seventh anniversary of his father's death in a road accident in Penang on Nov 25, 2019.
It was the third major loss to hit the family, following the death of Thanus's 17-year-old sister from kidney complications in May.
His mother, S. Sethra, 54, who suffered a stroke several years ago, was inconsolable as his body was brought home.
The incident also left his close friend, R. Vinod Kumar, 34, fighting for his life at a private hospital after suffering critical injuries.
Vinod's lungs had collapsed, one of his arms was shattered, and he remained in and out of consciousness under heavy sedation.
The two men were among six relatives and close friends who had gone out on three motorcycles about 4am on Tuesday. Thanus was riding pillion with Vinod.
They had planned to meet to discuss a family gathering to celebrate the new year.
They were less than a kilometre from home when they came across three vehicles — a Proton Waja, Volkswagen and Toyota Hilux — and several men believed to be cutting underground cables.
Thanus's cousin, D. Tachaaiyinan, 31, said the suspects scrambled into their vehicles when they spotted the group, while the Waja driver was loading the cut cables into the car.
"Thanus took out his phone and started recording them. When they saw us, they rushed into their vehicles and tried to speed off.
"Vinod who was on the motorcycle with Thanus, was in front of the Waja, which had two men inside.
"Instead of avoiding him, the driver rammed into them, causing both of them to fall," he said.
Tachaaiyinan, a self-employed caterer, said the Waja pinned Thanus and the motorcycle to the ground.
Vinod managed to move away, but Thanus remained unconscious on the road.
"I immediately went to help him, but the driver accelerated and ran over the motorcycle and Thanus.

"It happened within seconds. I managed to grab hold of the driver, but when I saw Thanus on the road bleeding badly, I let go and rushed to help Thanus," he said when met at the family home in Taman Damai Jaya.
Tachaaiyinan said the Hilux then reversed towards them, forcing the group to move out of its path.
All three vehicles sped off, with the Waja dragging the motorcycle along.
He said emergency responders arrived within five minutes after the group contacted the authorities.
Tachaaiyinan said Thanus had been staying with him, his mother and wife at Taman Damai Jaya, while Thanus's mother, grandfather and other siblings lived three houses away along Jalan Makmur 3.
He said Thanus had spent the previous week sleeping at his mother's house before knocking on his door at 4am that morning to invite him out.
"He told me he wanted to meet our relatives and discuss plans for the new year. We never imagined this would be our last outing together," he said.
Tachaaiyinan said Thanus had been supporting his family, including his mother, who had been bedridden since suffering a stroke.
