8ea9b1d2f0c6849f: NEW YORK, Nov 26 — S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s “AA” credit rating on watch for a potential downgrade on Wednesday, warning that the abrupt resignation and swift reinstatement of chief executive Jensen Huang revealed systemic deficiencies in management and board oversight at the world’s premier artificial intelligence chipmaker.

“We believe the long tenure of certain board ‌members may have compromised their independence. The company’s corporate governance practices may also not have kept pace with Nvidia’s rapid growth and its role as a critical global technology enabler,” the ratings agency said.

According to Reuters, S&P indicated it could downgrade Nvidia by one notch within the next 90 days, cautioning that a more severe cut could follow if continuing regulatory investigations inflict lasting damage on the company’s corporate reputation or commercial prospects.

The credit warning compounds an unprecedented period of executive instability in Silicon Valley. Nvidia directors reinstated Huang on Monday, barely a week after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over revelations of extramarital relationships with direct reports and a former executive at Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed.

The reversal drew intense criticism from corporate governance specialists and lawmakers, particularly after the board’s newly appointed chair had assured institutional investors that Huang would not return because his personal conduct breached the company’s code of conduct.

In announcing his return, Nvidia omitted reference to the workplace misconduct, stating instead that the decision was “based on US government input,” while an independent board committee continued probing reports surrounding foreign intelligence efforts.

The political pressure surrounding the reinstatement was underscored by reports that the US Department of Justice conducted no formal inquiry into Huang before President Donald Trump publicly lobbied for his return.

Federal authorities reportedly concluded there was no evidence he violated federal statutes based on existing export-smuggling investigations into client firms Super Micro and Megaspeed International, though prosecutors cautioned that the assessment remains fluid.

Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that a classified congressional briefing by the CIA, FBI, National Security Agency, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence found no indication that Beijing directed tech executive Alice Huang to target Jensen Huang.

While intelligence officers noted that Alice Huang maintained contact with China’s Ministry of State Security during the relationship and that her husband, Kang Wei, was an active intelligence asset, officials assessed that the affair was romantic rather than an orchestrated state intelligence operation.

Rival agency Moody’s struck a more pragmatic tone, affirming Nvidia’s Aa1 rating with a stable outlook. Moody’s argued that returning Huang to the helm eliminates critical leadership transition risks and stabilizes core operational execution, even as regulatory and board governance uncertainties persist.

Equity markets took S&P’s warning in stride, with Nvidia shares sliding nearly four per cent on Wednesday to extend a broader 38 per cent decline since early October, while debt insurance costs held steady.

The governance upheaval arrives as analysts scrutinise Nvidia’s circular financing arrangements across the technology sector. By aggressively bankrolling artificial intelligence startups, specialized cloud operators, and data centre developments that subsequently reinvest those capital injections into Nvidia’s proprietary computing hardware, the semiconductor giant faces heightened vulnerability to systemic shocks if broader industry spending cools.
4d7510a105797812: Terlebih dahulu, saya perlu memberitahu bahawa 'Tan Sri' dan 'Dato Seri' pada tajuk penulisan ini ialah anugerah kebesaran yang dipakai Presiden PAS Hadi Awang. Artikel ini sekadar menjelaskan apa yang dinyatakan beliau tempoh hari adalah salah.
Saya petik laporan FMT kelmarin. Kata Hadi partinya semakin mendapat sokongan golongan bukan Islam, namun golongan yang beliau maksudkan ialah mereka yang dia sifatkan sebagai 'tidak ekstrem'.
Jadi adakah Hadi menyifatkan semua orang bukan Islam yang tidak menyokong PAS golongan 'ekstrem'?

Apakah takrif 'ekstrem' menurut pandangan presiden PAS itu? Siapakah golongan 'tidak ekstrem' yang presiden PAS itu maksudkan? Saya kira MCA, MIC dan juga Gerakan, kerana Hadi pernah kata PAS boleh dan sudah bekerjasama dengan tiga parti itu.

Namun, penerimaan Hadi akan MCA dan MIC ialah berdasarkan dua parti itu komponen Barisan Nasional, dan PAS mempunyai persefahaman dengan BN sejak PRN Negeri Sembilan. Gerakan pula sememangnya komponen Perikatan Nasional. Maka, tidak bolehlah kita menyamakan sokongan tiga parti itu dengan sokongan masyarakat bukan Islam, kerana tiga parti itu tidak lagi mewakili komuniti itu secara menyeluruh.

Apa pun, menurut Hadi, PAS yakin mampu menewaskan PH pada PRU16 kelak berdasarkan 'keputusan memberangsangkan' dalam beberapa PRN baru-baru ini. Jelas beliau merujuk kepada PRN Johor, Negeri Sembilan dan Melaka.
Tetapi keputusan memberangsangkan di tiga PRN itu tercapai hasil kerjasama dengan Umno. Hakikatnya, gandingan PAS-Umno disokong pengundi Melayu, bukannya pengundi bukan Melayu bukan Islam.

Diakui Hadi banyak menyumbang kepada pencapaian bergaya itu apabila menyeru penyokong PAS mengundi BN. Kenyataan beliau bahawa wajib orang Islam sokong calon Islam diakui sebilangan besar pengundi Melayu. Bagaimanapun that same statement telah menyaksikan golongan bukan Islam bukan Melayu menjauhi PAS. Bukanlah rahsia mereka tidak senang dengan kenyataan Hadi, sedangkan ramai pemimpin bukan Melayu yang baik dan bersih. Bahkan, perasaan orang bukan Islam terguris apabila Hadi mendakwa orang bukan Islam sebagai punca gejala rasuah.
Jadi apabila Hadi kata PAS semakin dapat sokongan bukan Islam adalah sesuatu yang tidak betul.

Untuk double confirm pendapat saya itu, saya bertanya beberapa penyelidik yang membuat kaji selidik di lapangan semasa tiga PRN tempoh hari. Seorang daripada mereka memberitahu saya bahawa apa yang dikatakan Hadi itu tidak betul, menurut dapatan para penyelidik. Seorang lagi kata "finding saya: tak betul".
Ringkasnya, Hadi salah dalam rumusannya.

Kenyataan Hadi sememangnya pelik. Saya yang tidak berbekalkan hasil penyelidikan pun boleh rasa majoriti orang bukan lslam tidak sokong PAS, tidak kira 'ekstrem' atau 'tak ekstrem' (sekadar meminjam istilah Hadi).

Daripada mana Hadi dapat maklumat sehingga beliau boleh merumuskan sokongan bukan Islam kepada PAS semakin meningkat? Mustahil para penyelidik PAS tak tahu keadaan sebenar -- tak mungkin mereka tidak beri laporan tepat dan benar kepada presiden.
Adakah Hadi punya intel sendiri? Maklumlah presiden memang wajar ada banyak saluran maklumat tetapi apa yang beliau umumkan itu tidak betul.

Mungkinkah apa yang Hadi katakan itu bertujuan menyuntik semangat pemimpin dan ahli parti supaya mereka mempunyai keyakinan bagi menghadapi PRU kelak? Tetapi, bak dikata tadi, tentu mereka juga ada maklumat sendiri mengenai keadaan sebenar.
Atau mungkin Hadi sekadar main psywar untuk menakutkan pihak lawan, atau Hadi mahu menenangkan perasaan Umno yang mungkin gusar kenyataan Hadi akan membuatkan orang bukan Islam menjauhi PAS-Umno?
Mungkinkah juga untuk tenangkan perasaan ahli PAS sendiri yang memendam rasa tetapi risau kata-kata Hadi akan menyusahkan parti memikat hati pengundi bukan Islam?

Imbau kembali PRN Melaka. Tidak sampai 48 jam sebelum orang Melaka keluar mengundi, Hadi berucap di pentas grand finale BN-PN untuk memberi peringatan tentang pentingnya umat Islam keluar mengundi. OK, no problem with that.

Kata beliau, dalam Islam perkiraan politik dibuat berlandaskan faktor dosa dan pahala berbanding orang bukan Islam yang dituduhnya 'zalim'. Katanya lagi, kesan daripada orang Islam tidak keluar mengundi ialah 'orang lain' yang akan jadi pemerintah, dan menurut Hadi mereka akan bertindak mengikut perkiraan sendiri dan mengabaikan amanah yang diwajibkan Allah.
Siapakah 'orang lain' yang beliau maksudkan? Saya kira umum tahu.
Apapun beliau kata sebab itu orang Islam mesti tunaikan kewajipan mengundi untuk memimpin seluruh manusia. Do you think orang bukan Islam senang dengan kata-kata itu?
Apa lagi ini: "sejahat-jahat orang Islam seburuk-buruk orang Islam memerintah negeri, mereka tidak sezalim orang bukan Islam." Tuduhan ini memang menyakiti hati orang bukan Islam.

Menurut Malaysiakini, setiausaha politik kepada Hadi iaitu Syahir Sulaiman memberitahu portal berita itu bahawa kenyataan Hadi kononnya merujuk kepada apa yang berlaku dalam sejarah pemerintahan Islam.
Bagi saya, penjelasan itu sukar diterima kerana maksud dan sasaran Hadi memang jelas. Ia mencetuskan kemarahan orang bukan Islam termasuk parti yang mengaku sekutu PAS.

Menyusuli kenyataan Pejabat Presiden PAS yang mendakwa kata-kata Hadi dipetik di luar konteks, ini pada hemat saya tidak lebih daripada usaha damage control. Hakikatnya apa yang Hadi kata tidak boleh atau susah dipertahankan. Apatah lagi ada video ucapan.
Realitinya Hadi did say what he said. Soal luar konteks tidak timbul. Pejabat Presiden PAS pun tidak menafikan, cuma mendakwa kenyataan Hadi was taken out of context.

Mungkin Hadi mahu buktikan kepada semua pihak termasuk ahli parti bahawa kenyataannya tidak mendatangkan mudarat -- sebaliknya PAS semakin dapat sokongan orang bukan Islam meskipun facts and figures showed otherwise.
Kesimpulan terbaik dibuat seorang penganalisis politik, apabila berkata: "Kalau Hadi yang kata, yang pelik-pelik ni tak menghairankan."
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
1971fed7ee244905: WASHINGTON, Nov 26 — US GDP growth in the third quarter was revised strongly upwards on Wednesday, with the Commerce Department citing strong investment and consumer spending, as the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge hit a three-year high in October.

US GDP growth in the third quarter this year was estimated at 4.3 per cent at an annualized rate, the department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said, a rise of 0.9 percentage points from the previous estimate and much higher than market expectations.

“Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports,” the BEA said in a statement.

The US economy has shown resilient growth in recent months despite facing significant headwinds, including from President Donald Trump’s chaotic tariff policies and his war on Iran, which has driven up energy prices.

Also on Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge came in at a three-year high in October, according to BEA data, with a rise in energy prices accompanied by an increase in nondurable goods inflation.
The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index rose by 3.8 per cent year-on-year in October, the data showed, matching a three-year high set in May.
The US Federal Reserve has a long-term two-percent target for PCE inflation, one that it has missed for almost six years.
In September, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years in order to combat the persistent price increases, which have battered US households and businesses.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held rates steady at its last meeting in October, but with inflation continuing to run hot, it is likely to raise rates at its next confab in December.
The years of above-target inflation since the pandemic have hit US households hard, with current price levels more than 30 per cent higher than in 2020, as per the official Consumer Price Index.
Affordability was a key issue in this month’s midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by their rival Democrats.
The price increases have been driven by Trump’s tariffs, energy price increases due to the war on Iran and a massive investment boom in AI technology driving up demand for some goods.
Trump has defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom.
Economists warn that while consumer spending has remained strong, despite the high prices, there is a growing divide between lower- and higher-income households in the United States.
Beige Book’

The Fed’s latest “Beige Book,” released Wednesday, said US consumers grappling with high consumer prices have been “increasingly selective” in discretionary purchases. Auto sales weakened in a move the report attributed to higher energy prices, while lofty lending rates were a drag on the housing market.
On the positive side, the report said employment levels “rose slightly,” with contacts in several sectors citing “steady or rising labour demand.”
Of the 12 districts across the country, eight reported “slight to moderate” growth while four reported no change, the Fed report said.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said the fresh inflation data pointed to a likely rate hike in December, and possibly another a month later.
“America’s inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock,” she said. “The Federal Reserve has to act in December and likely January.”
She pointed out that while consumer spending did increase in absolute terms in October, it was flat once adjusted for inflation.

Ryan Sweet, chief global economist at Oxford Economics, said the strong GDP data would give Fed policymakers room to breathe when it comes to further rate hikes, which tend to cool economic activity as they tackle inflation.
“The tightening in financial market conditions, if sustained, will not have a noticeable impact on growth until the second half of next year,” he said. — AFP

23f83af51db231e9: Karim Ibrahim wants the police and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to investigate RM10 million he claims has gone missing from Malaysia Athletics (MA), along with more than RM500,000 allegedly missing from state associations.
These are grave allegations. But before the former MA president points investigators towards others, he must answer some uncomfortable questions about his own stewardship.
Karim says he secured RM10 million in sponsorship for athletics and now wants to know where the money went. Yet he was not an outsider watching from the sidelines.
He was at the helm of the national governing body when, by his own account, the sponsorship was secured.

If he brought in that money, he should be able to identify the sponsor, explain the terms of the agreement, state how much MA actually received and account for what the funds were supposed to support.
There is also a fundamental difference between securing a sponsorship package worth RM10 million and having that entire sum deposited into MA’s accounts.

Was the figure a contractual commitment, the total value of a sponsorship deal or money actually paid to the association? Were payments made in one lump sum or released in stages against agreed programmes?
The questions become even more pressing because nobody appears to know who this supposedly generous sponsor was.

A sports body landing RM10 million would normally shout it from the rooftops. Its leaders would hold a press conference, parade the corporate partner and trumpet the deal as a vote of confidence in the sport.
They would tell athletes, coaches and the public what the money would deliver. Such a windfall would be a major achievement, not something to keep under wraps.
Yet there appears to have been no public fanfare, no named corporate partner and no clear account of the initiative the money was meant to support.
Who put up the sponsorship? Was the agreement ever announced? What programmes did it fund, and what did MA promise in return?

A sponsor committing such a sum would also expect answers. It would want to know whether the money had reached its intended programmes, whether agreed targets were being met and how the association had used the funds.

Did MA provide progress reports or financial accounts? Did the sponsor ask for updates? If payments came in instalments, what evidence of progress did MA have to provide before receiving the next tranche?
These are not peripheral details. They go to the heart of whether the RM10 million deal existed in the form Karim now describes, how much money changed hands and what happened to it.
The sponsorship agreement, payment records, bank statements and audited accounts should provide the answers.
Karim should put the details on the table rather than leave the public to chase a figure without a name attached to it.
Serious allegations need hard evidence

Karim’s claim that some money went into personal accounts is even more explosive. It suggests possible misappropriation, yet the interview reported by Scoop offers no transaction details, names, dates or documents to substantiate it.
Which accounts received the money? How much was transferred? Who authorised the payments? What evidence led him to conclude that the transactions were improper?
The same scrutiny must apply to his claim that more than RM500,000 has disappeared from state associations.
He cites RM18,000 involving Selangor athletics, more than RM100,000 linked to fixed deposits and almost RM200,000 involving the national association.
But he does not explain how these figures were established or whether they refer to missing funds, unexplained withdrawals, disputed transactions or accounting discrepancies.

These are different things. A fixed deposit that cannot immediately be traced does not, by itself, prove that money has been stolen. Nor does an unexplained entry in an account establish that someone pocketed the funds.

Karim says he knows about the alleged irregularities because he examined state association accounts as MA president. If so, he should identify the associations, the periods involved and the transactions that triggered his suspicions.
He should also say whether he raised these concerns with MA’s executive council. Checks with council members indicate that they are unaware of the allegations and shocked by the claims.
If Karim had formally alerted them, there should be a record of when he did so and what action followed.

The executive council will have an opportunity to address the allegations when it meets on Nov 29. Its members should use the meeting to seek a full account of the sponsorship Karim claims to have secured, examine the financial records and establish whether anyone raised concerns about the transactions while he was president.
The association cannot afford to let such serious claims drift without a formal response.
There is another question he cannot duck. As MA president and a signatory to its cheques, Karim had the authority to seek financial records, question payments and demand explanations.
Did he exercise that responsibility? Did he ask for an audit, challenge suspicious transactions or alert the relevant authorities while he was still in office?
If he did, he should produce the correspondence and explain what happened. If he did not, he must explain why he waited until after his disqualification to raise such serious allegations.

Karim says he wants the police and MACC to investigate. If he has evidence of wrongdoing, he should put it before them. Has he lodged a report with either agency, the sports commissioner or MA? Has he handed over the documents on which his claims rest?
Calling for an investigation is easy. Giving investigators something concrete to pursue is another matter.

The timing deserves scrutiny, too. Karim has made these claims after his disqualification from the MA presidency. That does not make them false, and MA cannot brush them aside simply because of who is making them.
But if he knew of suspected financial wrongdoing while leading the association, why did he not expose it then?
MA has been asked to respond to the allegations. Its account is essential, and it must answer for any financial irregularities that the evidence establishes.
Any credible evidence of wrongdoing deserves an independent investigation, regardless of who is implicated.

But accountability cannot be a one-way demand. Karim is entitled to ask where the money went. He must also account for what he knew, what he did and what records he left behind when he led the association.
He cannot demand that others explain the money while leaving his own stewardship beyond scrutiny.
If there are culprits, name them and produce the evidence. But Karim must start by answering for his own time at the helm.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
0c6bc9d95e3a2ca7: Entah berapa banyak agaknya jumlah wang syiling 50 sen yang saya genggam, turut terisi mengembung saku di kedua-dua belah seluar. Semata untuk menghubungi Pak Samad Said dari telefon awam berwarna kuning yang sobek berkarat di bucu.

Setiap kali dering berlaga di gegendang menalun, jantung saya tidak berhenti berdetak bergetar dengan keras. Setiap kali juga, suara Kak Rashidah menyambut di hujung. Setiap kali itu juga saya tidak dapat menduga rasanya. Saya dengan sedikit segan akan merengek meminta bicara dengan Bapak. Kak Rashidah akan bersuara lembut, memanggilkan; "Pak, Faisal..."
Seperti selalunya Bapak akan meladeni saya sehingga ke syiling 50 sen saya yang terakhir. Malam melewat, tetapi kesungguhan Bapak kekal mengawal.

Saya mungkin terlalu mementingkan diri. Saya ingin melahap segala ilmu dan pengalaman Bapak untuk diri saya sendiri. Seolah saya ingin menyedut apa sahaja dari sosok tubuh yang kecil itu tanpa nanti-nanti. Saya tidak memikirkan apakah perasaan Kak Rashidah, isteri Bapak. Atau keperluan Az, anaknya yang masih bersekolah.

Di kuburan, tengah hari Rabu; dengan kawanan merpati menyinggah dan halai-balai penziarah, saya menangis memburam kaca mata untuk akhirnya berterima kasih kepada Kak Rashidah yang juga sudah sendu dalam telekung syahdu, "Terima kasih Kak kerana meminjamkan saya Bapak, seluruh alam remaja saya terbangun sebetulnya adalah kerana Bapak."
Kepada Az, saya tersekat-sekat mengaku dalam dakapannya, "Terima kasih Az kerana berkongsi Bapak dengan saya."

Sebaik beroleh maklumat mengenai Bapak, saya bersegera ke Hospital Kuala Lumpur. Hati kecil saya sedang menafikan, bahawa detik itu sedang menghampiri. Serasa bergegar stereng kenderaan, ikut berhenjutan dengan bahu. Langit keruh, dan saya membayangkan wira bukit bangsa sedang terdampar. Perlahan-lahan semuanya bergulungan datang semula, bagai ombak kenangan yang melanda berkali-kali.

Tiga puluh lebih tahun lalu, Bapak di tiang Masjid Negara, menghabiskan juzuk-juzuk al-Quran seusai sembahyang Jumaat, dan membiarkan saya menanti terperuk di sebalik tembok. Selalu akan ada telaah buku. Saya akan berteleku mendengar nama Mo Yan, Gabriel Garcia Marquez, Manuel Puig, Rabindranath Tagore, Rumi, Iqbal, Patrick White, serta sejumlah pengarang besar Rusia dengan hati-hati, meminta disimbah segala titah untuk menyelesaikan naskah-naskah itu. Demi Allah, Bapak sungguh pemurah.

Buku-buku itu, saya selalu terlongo, akan berbau harum dari toko. Naskhah yang masih semerbak ditandatangani, dengan jeling saya yang puas. Selesai asar, kami akan bergerak ke Mcggoo Deli, di nombor 85, Jalan Tun H S Lee. Anak-anak kru kafe itu sudah menanti dengan senyum. Saya selalu akan memesan croissant disumbat tuna. Kak Rashidah akan tiba, dengan kemanisan yang tidak putus. Saya akan mendengar Bapak memberitahu, "Shidah saya tertinggal payung, atau Shidah saya terlupa akan itu, akan ini..." Sentiasa ada aneka kekesalan. Kak Rashidah akan memandang saya dengan mata bening, "Tak apalah, nak buat macam mana."

Kadang-kadang sesi perguruan tersebut akan tergendala beberapa minggu, kerana Bapak ke Teluk Melano atau entah ke Miri, barangkali, selalu dengan Marzuki Ali. Bapak akan mengusik, "Ya, ada buku sementara Bapak tiada, jangan terlalu iri."

Buku-buku pemberian Bapak itu selain mahal, terlalu susah untuk saya baca. Ia sungguh sasterawi. Ia dalam bahasa Inggeris. Kamus ringkas saya tidak menampung kalimat langka yang dijejerkan. Selaku siswa syariah yang bergulat dengan bahasa Arab, halaman buku yang Bapak suguhkan sangat membikin lara. Bertahun, akhirnya makan tahun tanpa saya sedari bahasa Inggeris saya meluru membaik kerana 'The English Patient', 'A Fine Balance', atau 'The Remains of the Day'.

Bapak mencabar saya menulis sebuah karya untuk menewaskan rekodnya yang menghasilkan Salina di usia sangat muda. Saya memberikan Bapak dua, 'Perempuan Politikus Melayu' dan 'Cinta Hari-hari Rusuhan'. Saya sangsi Bapak membacanya. Sehingga beberapa bulan kemudian Johan Jaafar mengulas novel tersebut di akhbar Inggeris begitu memuji. Saranan yang kelihatannya datang daripada Bapak. Atau bagaimana Othman Puteh mengangkat karya lainnya, sebagai sebuah roman meruntun jiwa, yang akhirnya diakui oleh Othman, juga atas anjuran Bapak.

Pernah saya menanyakan Bapak, "Mengapa Bapak menulis yang itu sahaja -- Perang Dunia Kedua, konfrontasi, dan kekacauan seorang lelaki dalam Hujan Pagi." Bapak bersengaja membalas, "Kerana Bapak tidak masuk universiti seperti Faisal Tehrani. Kekayaan Bapak adalah pengalaman itu..."

Sekali Bapak ingin ke Melaka, untuk menziarahi ibu bapa saya. Kata Bapak, dia ingin mengerti latar saya. Seolah-olah saya beroleh seluruh hadiah yang ada di dunia. Ibu saya mengukus ikan, abah mengambil cuti dua hari dan mencabut rumput di laman; dan saya melihat Bapak santai berbicara hal politik, ehwal sejagat dan macam-macam lagi. Dari stesen bas Melaka, Bapak enggan menaiki Bas Wira, sebaliknya kami berbeca. Di hujung ziarah itu Bapak mengatakan, "Oh ya, Bapak tahu Faisal akan tumbuh lagi."

Pada tahun 1996, Bapak dilamar untuk menulis drama pentas. Saya melihat-lihat nestapa Bapak mengarang perihal Tengku Seindahkuno, yang akhirnya diberi jolokan 'T Pinkie'. Saya ingin sekali mengekori Bapak ke Singapura menonton pementasan itu tetapi pasport saya sudah tidak bernyawa lagi, dan tiket ke Singapura suntuk dalam kepala. Tahu-tahu Bapak memadankan saya dengan Ladin Nuawi, "Nanti Faisal ke Singapura ya, belajar sesuatu, dan mengerti. Ladin akan memasti Faisal selamat serba-serbi."
Begitu sahaja saya beroleh ilmu pentas daripada Pak Samad.

Dalam tahun 1998 dan 1999, di tengah gelora reformasi, Pak Samad mengarang 'Al Amin'. Puisi panjang berirama dan beramsal. Bapak dibayar bulan demi bulan, dan setiap kali hari wangnya tiba, saya akan mengikut Bapak ke ATM. Akan ada ringgit seratus dua, croissant dan beberapa buku lagi, kali ini Dante dan ada juga siri jilid Naquib Mahfodz. Dalam tempoh itu saya berguru dengan Bapak segala mengenai puisi.

Apabila 'Ingin Jadi Nasrallah' (2010) diterbitkan, Bapak menulis ransang sari. Bapak mencatat begini, "Yang selalu kedengaran ialah suara jernih di malam hening -- jelas dan langsung. Saya kira, memang itulah kekuatan utama Faisal Tehrani sebagai penulis (kini penyair) walaupun dengan himpunan puisinya yang sejemput itu dia sempat hadir menegap di situ. Dengan suara sederhana, berani bersikap, subur berakar, malah garang; Faisal Tehrani mula hadir berkesan dalam dunia puisi mutakhir. Penyair tulen biasanya menghantar isyarat dan ibarat sebelum sesebuah negara mudarat."
Saya dibaja, disiram; ada semaian yang tidak pernah putus.

Setelah saya ke Pulau Pinang berguru dengan Shahnon Ahmad, beliau mungkin cemburu sering mengajuk Bapak. Misalnya Cikgu mengatakan Bapak kurang berani, terlalu berlapik dan berkias dalam karya. Akan selalu ada sindir perli Cikgu. Sering saya rasa kurang senang. Namun kedua-duanya guru, jika mereka bersaing atau saling mencurigai, mengapa pula saya harus memasuki daerah mereka. Tentu, tatkala itu Shahnon namanya panas kerana menulis satira menghakimi kuasawan.

Bapak beroleh gelaran Datuk pada tahun 1997 oleh Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka. Saya ternyata rimas dengan gelaran itu dan mempertikaikan, semacam merasa-rasa apa telahan Cikgu Shahnon itu semakin benar. Bapak menjelaskan kegusaran saya, "Akan tiba masanya gelar ini akan Bapak gunakan untuk merebut kembali apa yang telah diambil daripada kita."
Lama kemudian, di Bangi, Cikgu Shahnon menggamit saya di Seksyen 3, dan membisikkan dituruti tawa, "Selepas Cikgu tiada, Samad kamu itu akan melakukan lebih dari apa yang telah Cikgu lakukan."

Ternyata firasat Cikgu Shahnon benar. Bapak kelak akan memimpin bantahan terhadap PPSMI, serta gerakan Bersih 2.0. Lantas mendepani baton FRU, belantan ganas polis, semburan gas pemedih mata dan berdiri tegak di hadapan pelbagai demonstrasi (Bapak menamakannya tunjuk kasih, dan bukan tunjuk perasaan).

Sehingga hari ini, Bapak satu-satunya sasterawan yang meletakkan seni itu sebagai sebahagian daripada kehidupan jelata. Hanya seorang sasterawan berani turun ke jalan raya. Namanya A Samad Said, hatta saya tidak akan berdaya melakukannya.

Ketika tahun-tahun pengajian saya di UKM, Bapak akan sering bertanya dan mendoakan agar saya mendirikan rumah tangga. Pada Oktober 2009, Bapak ke Melaka sekali lagi, kali ini ditemani Kak Rashidah. Mereka menaiki bas menghadiri kenduri perkahwinan saya di Dewan Hang Tuah. Terdapat sehampar sketsa, dianugerahkan buat saya. Ia lakaran sebatang pohon yang katanya, 'akar terbenam ke bumi'.

Di antara tahun-tahun 2012-2017 saya mengalami depresi. Berat badan saya bertambah, tekanan membahana. Nama saya diburukkan oleh Zahid Hamidi, mufti Perlis dan pentadbiran Najib Razak. Karya saya dilarang, Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka tiba-tiba memutuskan hubungan. Sebagai pengarang sepenuh masa, saya kehilangan mata pencarian.

Bapak sudah mahir menggunakan emel, dan Bapak menjawab begini dalam balasannya bertarikh 6 Jun 2012; "Bapak berdoa ia akan berakhir dengan baik. Betapa pun, jika buruk keadaannya, janganlah pula tergesa melawan. Teliti dan timbang dulu kesannya, termasuk kesannya terhadap kedudukanmu di varsiti. Walaupun, sebenarnya, sangat wajar dilawan."

Saya memfailkan permohonan semakan kehakiman di Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur pada 29 Jun 2015 untuk buku-buku saya yang diharamkan. Keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi pada Ogos 2016 ialah Hakim Hanipah Farikullah menolak permohonan tersebut dan memutuskan bahawa tindakan Kementerian Dalam Negeri adalah munasabah. Tiada seorang pengarang Malaysia pun bersama-sama dengan saya. Serasa seisi bumi mentertawa. Mereka malah menghindari saya.
Kecuali Pak Samad Said dan Kak Rashidah datang menaiki bas dan teksi untuk memberi sokongan.

Segala ombak kenangan itu menghempas pantai benak saya berulangan kali. Semakin stereng kereta saya bergegar tatkala memasuki petak parkir hospital. Di wad Mawar, Az dengan lesung pipit menyambut, dan aduh senyum serta kelembutan Kak Rashidah terpapar lagi, "Faisal masuklah, Faisal sapa Bapak... kalau Bapak buka mata dan bangun."

Saya membelai rambut Bapak, saya ingin mengucup tangan Bapak seperti selalunya akan tetapi saya khuatir ada jarum terlekat, serta topeng oksigen Bapak akan terlorot. Saya meronta-ronta ingin meneriak nama Bapak. Saya ingin memberitahunya bahawa seluruh dunia saya sebetulnya pernah terbangun oleh sosok kecil ini.

Seisi alam remaja saya begitu bergantung kepadanya. Saya terngiang-ngiang kembali tawa Bapak, dan cungap kami menyusuri laluan dari Masjid Negara, merentasi Daya Bumi ke Pasar Seni. Saya tahu detik masanya seakan tiba. Saya tidak memahami mengapa Kak Rashidah semacam tenang dan aman-aman sahaja. Saya merintih di celah bacaan Yasin, saya terngiang kembali kasih Bapak. Betapa banyak dikau memberi. Betapa banyak.

Di kuburan, tatkala mereka mengambus tanah di pusaramu, saya berasa ingin menerkam dan menjeritkan, jangan ayohai tolong jangan dulu. Nusa bangsa ini masih memerlukan keberanianmu. Kita barangkali akan turun lagi ke jalanan. Saya masih ingin melaungkan, ternyata banyak belum kita laksanakan kerana kuasawan dan korupsi masih bermaharajalela.

Tetapi saya menyaksikan semua yang hadir membiarkan kepal tanah keras itu menelangkup. Talkin dibaca. Mereka kemudian menyirami air di atas kuburan itu. Perlahan-lahan saya melihat pusara Bapak sempurna. Bapak bersemadi, dan saya tidak percaya.
Serasa sunyi dan sendiri. Ada sekawanan merpati tiba-tiba melayah rendah, hingar-bingar teman dan saudara. Beberapa pembesar dan orang terkenal bertingkah seperti biasa.

Pun ombak kenangan menerpa, dan Ya Allah, kaca mata saya memburam dan saya mendengar suara Bapak, sayup-sayup di hujung gagang telefon. Lirih tetapi padat, tergagap tetapi teguh; ketawa Bapak. Langit saya lihat makin keruh, membawa gerimis.
Kembali di gegendang telinga saya, denting syiling 50 sen yang segenggam itu jatuh ke dalam tampungan telefon awam, sekeping demi sekeping.
Sehingga ke syiling terakhir.
Suara Bapak terputus tiba-tiba.

099ddd8378bba93f: At 5pm on June 28, 1982, a research reactor in Bangi called TRIGA PUSPATI reached its criticality for the first time, ushering Malaysia into the nuclear age. Forty-four years on it is still running, yet we have never produced a single unit of nuclear electricity.

That's not for want of trying. Under then prime minister Najib Razak, Malaysia planned two nuclear plants by 2021 and set up the Malaysia Nuclear Power Corporation in January 2011, two months before a tsunami crippled Japan's Fukushima Daiichi plant.
Then in 2018, Dr Mahathir Mohamad's new government scrapped the plan, citing a lack of expertise and worries over radioactive waste.

Now nuclear is back. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's 13th Malaysia Plan names it a viable clean power source, with implementation targeted from 2031, and Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Chang Lih Kang told Parliament last month that no decision on technology or construction will come until four key studies are completed within 12 months.
I can't help but feel we are about to study our way into another lost decade. We need nuclear more than ever, and here's why.
We are living on a diet of coal

While we dithered, coal took over. According to energy think tank Ember, coal's share of Malaysia's power generation rose from 6% in 2000 to 43% in 2024, and Reuters' analysis of grid data shows it supplied 58.6% of Peninsular Malaysia's electricity last year.
Most of it isn't even ours, with a record 36.3 million tonnes of thermal coal imported in 2025, about three-quarters of it from Indonesia.

We pay for it with our lungs and our climate. Oxford's Our World in Data project estimates coal kills nearly 25 people for every terawatt-hour of electricity it produces, and deputy prime minister Fadillah Yusof has said coal power accounts for nearly half of our national emissions.

We have rightly promised to retire coal by 2044, but here's the kicker: economy minister Akmal Nasrullah Nasir said in September that we expect to add about 9GW of gas-fired capacity, swapping one fossil fuel for another.

There's a cleaner swap, and it doesn't get any cleaner than nuclear. A 2021 United Nations Economic Commission for Europe study found nuclear had the lowest lifecycle emissions of any power source it studied, at 5.1 to 6.4 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilowatt-hour, against 751 to 1,095 grams for coal.
Sure, solar should still do the heavy lifting by day. But to replace coal we need something that runs at 3am every night of the year, whatever the weather, and nuclear does exactly that.
The fears don't survive the data
Many Malaysians hear "nuclear" and think of Chernobyl. Yet per unit of electricity, Our World in Data finds nuclear causes 99.8% fewer deaths than coal.

Even after Fukushima, the UN's scientific committee on radiation found that "no adverse health effects among Fukushima residents have been documented that could be directly attributed to radiation exposure".

The waste is smaller than most imagine too, with the US Department of Energy saying all the spent fuel America's commercial reactors have produced since the 1950s could fit on a single American football field, stacked less than 10 metres deep.
On expertise, International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Mariano Grossi said in June that "there are many people in Malaysia who know nuclear technology and know what a nuclear reactor is".
So how do we get it right this time? Three things.
1. Set a decision date that outlives elections
Putrajaya should commit now to naming its reactor technology and first site within three months of the four studies landing, making the reports a starting gun rather than a resting place.
It should also give the programme its own act of Parliament, because a programme that takes more than a decade to deliver cannot be at the mercy of every new Cabinet.
2. Buy proven, and buy in a series

The United Arab Emirates shows what a first-timer can do. It began building its Barakah plant in July 2012, and today four identical Korean-designed reactors supply 25% of its electricity, with cost, time and labour falling by 40% between the first unit and the fourth.
We should do the same, ordering several identical units of a design already operating elsewhere rather than becoming any vendor's guinea pig.
3. Build the workforce now

Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal says many nuclear engineering graduates from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia now work in unrelated jobs, while Fadillah says quite a number of Malaysians work at French reactors.

MyPower, the agency coordinating the programme, should track these engineers down, and every cooperation deal we sign with France or the US should guarantee training places for Malaysians. Turkey, Wan Fayhsal notes, will switch on its first plant next year, 17 years after proposing it, so he is spot on: "Start today."

The little reactor in Bangi has been running since 1982, proof that Malaysians can be trusted with the atom. Every year we wait is another year of burning imported coal, so when the studies land, what Putrajaya needs is not another study but a date, a design and the courage to stick to both.

6e65d2141bfd18bf: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites.

The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.”

The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union.
SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less.
Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.”
The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request.

“SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters.
Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions.
Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “peak insanity.”

Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so.
Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create.

Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained.
Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites.

Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029.

Down on Earth, meanwhile, scientists trying to observe the universe continue to bemoan the obstructions caused by mega-constellations of broadband-beaming satellites. Proposals from across the USA, China, Europe and India currently call for around 100,000 satellites. SpaceX’s proposed million orbiters could run workloads which help us to understand the mysteries of the universe while also making them hard to see from down here. ®

de935a0c3aeb9eef: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems.

The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23.
It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020.
However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted.

Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords.

The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers, targeted more than 100 water systems, with incidents reported across at least 12 states, and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers.
According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17.

Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. A CISA advisory from July describes this technique:

The authoring agencies observed Iranian-affiliated APT actors using several foreign-based IP addresses to access internet-facing PLCs manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and potentially other manufactured PLCs [T0883]. The actors used leased, third-party hosted infrastructure and manufacturers’ PLC programming software to connect to misconfigured victim PLCs. Inbound malicious traffic has been observed targeting PLC devices on the following ports: 44818, 2222, 102, and 502, as well as targeting modems on port 22.
These cellular modems, often installed by third-party contractors, frequently aren’t documented.

Unsurprisingly, the top recommendation for water utilities is to find every cellular modem in the environment, including those installed by contractors, make sure they aren’t exposed to the open internet, and put a gateway with multifactor authentication (MFA) in front of them to stop would-be intruders from gaining access via the modem and controller combo.

“Water utilities are spending time and money fixing the vulnerabilities they're told to worry about,” Securin CEO Srinivas Mukkamala said in a statement. “Meanwhile, attackers are getting in through equipment nobody knew was connected or passwords nobody bothered to change.” ®

2a494ad604ec9734: In what sounds like an avian riff on The Wire, scientists equipped seabirds with audio recorders in order to listen in on their interactions with fishing vessels across the world’s oceans, according to a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances.

The approach exposed a large number of so-called “unseen” vessels that did not have their location trackers switched on. Many vessels are required to continuously signal their location using the Automatic Identification System (AIS), which openly broadcasts a ship’s location, similar to flight tracking. But AIS can be disabled for legitimate reasons—such as evading pirates—or with more nefarious motivations, such as concealment of illegal fishing activities.

The new study was not designed to interrogate why any particular vessel switched off its AIS tracker. However, the discovery that seabirds are regularly interacting with unseen ships can shed light on broader efforts to monitor commercial fisheries, while also revealing new insights about seabird behavior, especially their risk of becoming “bycatch” when they are fatally trapped in fishing gear.

Unseen vessel activity “is concerning, or at least important, regardless of whether it's legal or illegal,” said Jonathan Rutter, a postdoctoral research fellow at the University of Oxford who led the study, in a call with 404 Media. He added that the recordings were not intended to be used for law-enforcement or surveillance, but that this line of research could become a “powerful tool for improving risk assessment” by recording seabird-vessel interactions that would otherwise be off the map.

Scientists have previously attached audio recorders to birds, such as penguins, to better understand their vocalizations and behavior, and teams have also probed seabird-vessel interactions with bird-borne radar.

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Rutter and his colleagues were inspired to combine these approaches by attaching audio recorders to three seabird species—the northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel—which all frequently interact with fishing vessels. The team tracked the movements of the birds with GPS, and then analyzed whether the audio overlapped with AIS data at the same time and location during recorded interactions.

The recordings showed that about 32 percent of the audio captured by seven gannets in the North Atlantic were from ships with their trackers off, while 12 percent of the audio captured by four shearwaters in the Mediterranean Sea were from unseen vessels. The one petrel in the study interacted with vessels in the South Pacific, but its geolocation device was damaged, so it was not possible to calculate how many ships it encountered had their trackers off.

Rutter noted that the shearwaters were likely often interacting with smaller Mediterranean fishing boats that are not legally required to keep trackers on. However, the gannets encountered larger commercial vessels that are obligated to keep trackers active. While the researchers made a very conservative estimate that these birds visited unseen vessels for about one-third of the total duration of their daily encounters (or, about 22 minutes out of 68 minutes), it may well exceed half of that time.

“The fact that we found at least one third, and probably more than one half, of the audio detections being unseen was pretty surprising,” Rutter said. “This is not the same thing as saying that half of vessels are unseen; it's half of the time that gannets go to vessels, those vessels are unseen.”

“There are multiple reasons this could be,” he continued. “It could be illegal disabling, but at the same time, it could be poor satellite reception. There are lots of reasons that AIS can be off, and we want to emphasize that illegal fishing is a possibility, but that is not actually what we're showing. It's showing that there's a lot we're not seeing.”

Seabirds are attracted to fishing vessels to feed on discarded catch, but many perish during these encounters after becoming tangled in lines or caught on baited hooks. Rutter and his colleagues hope that their study could help to prevent these deadly incidents, while also providing a new tool for monitoring unseen vessel activity.

While this approach could enable real-time vessel detection, the team urged “caution in the use of animals as a fisheries surveillance tool, lest fishers come to mistrust scientists and/or marine animals themselves,” according to the study.

Though environmental and commercial interests are often at odds, there is plenty of collaboration between fisheries and conservation scientists with the goal of sustainable and healthy long-term fish stock. Fisheries that adhere to regulations also have an interest in working with researchers to combat illegal activity by competitors.

In addition, these audio recordings offer a new way to eavesdrop on wild seabird behavior. For example, the petrel’s recordings captured distinct landing and takeoff sequences previously observed in albatrosses, opening a new avenue of research into the flight patterns of this species. The recordings also highlight how human activity has upended food webs, as seabirds have become dependent on fishing vessel waste as a major source of food.

“One of the advantages of this is that we can understand in a more unbiased way how much [seabirds] actually interact with vessels—every day, multiple times a day for all the species we looked at actually, which is crazy if you think about it,” Rutter said.
“They're going out every day and just visiting boats all the time, and that shows the impact that we have on them as humans is really changing their feeding ecology,” he concluded.

b946c695c0817290: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing.
EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips.
Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools.
The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear.
Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology.
This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy.
“Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said.
We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area.

The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process.
For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025.

So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms.

“Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.”
This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live.
The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market.

We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

629cbfde7a723305: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024.

DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision.

Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same.

"Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width."
Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit.

Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits.

The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer."

Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing.

Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts.

Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

483f64d5371ececf: Ukraine has been executing a series of successful strikes against Russian assets around the world. Ukrainian forces disabled a Russian cargo vessel off the coast of Finland, and sunk a Russian corvette, the Merkury, along with damaging another cargo vessel, in Libyan waters. These attacks, in the aftermath of Ukraine’s severe damage to the Kerch Strait Bridge in Russian-occupied Crimea, have created hope among Ukraine’s allies. The year 2026 hasn’t advanced Ukraine’s goal of ending the war. A stagnant battlefront, increased Russian aerial attacks and a recalcitrant American president have increased the burdens on Ukraine’s government and its people. Russia hasn’t had a good year either. More than 400,000 Russians have been killed in the war — and potentially as many as 700,000. For Ukraine to have any chance of winning, it must increase the pressure on Russian leader Vladimir Putin’s government. Making Russian assets vulnerable globally is one way to do it. The international dimension Since its outset, the Russia-Ukraine conflict has had an international dimension. Ukraine’s allies, both prior to and after Russia’s full-fledged invasion in 2022, rushed supplies to Ukraine in its moment of need. Providing aid to Ukraine has continued for the past four years, despite disruptions caused by United States President Donald Trump’s involvement in the negotiation process. The supplies provided by Ukraine’s allies are critical to its success. While the fighting is conducted by the Ukrainian people and Ukraine has increased domestic arms production, outside supplies are crucial in a number of areas — notably, air defence. Equally important is the economic aid Ukraine’s allies have and continue to provide the country. Given the size differential between Russia and Ukraine and how hard the war has hit the Ukrainian economy, economic aid allows Ukraine to provide basic services to its citizens. Initially, Russia did not court outside support to the same extent as Ukraine, as it believed it would achieve a rapid victory over its adversary. Once the reality of the conflict became clear, Russia turned to the international community for support. That support has taken many forms. Iran and North Korea have been among Russia’s top supporters, providing drones and soldiers. Other countries, most notably China, have provided an economic lifeline to Russia, allowing it access to their markets in an effort to stave off the worst impacts of the economic sanctions Ukraine’s allies have imposed on the Russians. Countries in Central Asia and the Middle East have also served Russia as important intermediaries for acquiring sanctioned materials. Targeting support In a conflict that is increasingly defined by attrition, it’s been necessary for both Ukraine and Russia to rally their allies. The demands of industrialized warfare and the production of necessary armaments means neither country can produce what’s needed on their own. Because both sides are receiving critical support in this industrialized conflict, the war has reached an equilibrium. In their current states, neither side is likely to achieve a decisive breakthrough to rapidly end the fighting. For both Ukraine and Russia, that means targeting their adversary’s international allies is necessary to win the conflict. The least risky form of targeting enemy support, and among the most important, is by constructing narratives while delegitimizing those of your opponent. Ukraine has focused on Russia’s aggression and its violation of international norms and laws. The focus on international law is particularly important for Ukraine given Russian accusations that the West has flouted international norms for decades; Russia uses western association with Ukraine to gain support in the Global South. Russia has put forward several narratives to justify the war, ranging from defending itself from NATO imperialist expansion to its factually questionable claims of the Ukrainian state’s genocide against ethnic Russians in Ukraine. Russia had some early successes from these narratives, making political gains in Africa and earning support among far-right European parties. Narrative campaigns, however, typically unfold over a long time frame. As both Ukraine and Russia seek immediate ways to boost morale and undermine their adversary, direct military operations abroad have become all the more significant. Read more: Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s removal of two top defence officials highlights the role of morale in long wars Attacking the secure ‘rear’ In military terms, the rear is the area furthest from the enemy and ideally secure from military threat. For both Ukraine and Russia, this area has been other countries. While Russia and Ukraine cannot attack the assets of other countries directly, they can and do engage in espionage against other countries. For Russia, these efforts have focused on destabilizing Europe using drones and other assets via attacks that that are easily deniable. Russia also seeks to create pressure through violating European air space. The more Russia destabilizes Europe, Ukraine’s primary ally, the better its chances in the conflict. For Ukraine, Russia’s aspirations to be a so-called Great Power mean its network is global — so Ukrainian special operation forces and intelligence agencies strike at Russian assets abroad where possible. These range from attacks in nearby areas, like the Baltics, to Africa and beyond. Read more: Putin wanted to make Russia great again. Instead, Ukraine is the new rising power in Europe While news agencies view this development as widening the conflict, and the United Nations may wish to prevent the conflict from going global, the reality is it’s been a global conflict since before 2022. The strikes in Libya and the Baltic, and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy immediate acknowledgement of Ukraine’s role, is just making it public. a1a9de6fe232eb4d: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing.
Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says.

The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."

Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported.
The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections.

The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing."
Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated.
Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing.

The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737, a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network."

NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on.

Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

2a99f168595cd5f3: In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.

Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.

Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?

If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.

If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.

This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report. That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google (18%), Amazon (16%), and Microsoft (25%). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.

And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.

This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.

It’s not new for large industrial facilities to supply their own power. Chemical plants often have natural-gas infrastructure on-site to generate electricity and heat, for example (though they’re generally connected to the grid as well). Mining operations are often remote, requiring an off-grid power source.

But the desire to come online quickly means there could be a massive boom in off-grid power plants for data centers. Over 100 such facilities have been proposed in the US, with a total capacity of 115 gigawatts (that’s more than double the entire peak power demand of California). The vast majority of these sites have been proposed since the beginning of 2025.

There are alternative ways to help meet growing electricity demand: Wind and solar are inexpensive options, and pairing them with batteries could improve their reliability, for example. I’ve also written before about demand flexibility—efforts to limit power drawn from the grid when demand is high.
Right now, though, the evidence continues to stack up that the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom.
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.

83211bcc1b327541: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October.

Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars.

There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design."
The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth.
Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate.

Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit.
Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space.
NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module.
"Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said.
The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge. Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft.

4a86565e43195090: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons.
Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved.

The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window.

Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142
The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote.

Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums, where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair.
Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate.
Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things.

For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window."
Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong.
The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®
c131d93ba57f0b89: One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history: cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.

The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.
c7a5869b3d7038ed: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round.
The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation.

Like its predecessor, Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language, in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files.
Dirty data

The revised benchmark now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories.

The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request.
A 30-minute limit was set for each task.

Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories.

Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them.
Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks.
Leaderboard Shakeup

When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent.
Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however.

In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models.
Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials.
In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy.
(Kotlin users will pay dearly for the extra sliver of Anthropic accuracy: The average cost of Fable completing a Kotlin cleanup task runs $2.38, while Opus could do the job for $0.68.)
Gaming the boss

One possible interpretation of these disparate numbers is that models are drawing from their own knowledge bases instead of reasoning from scratch. Whether this is cheating or the models simply working as intended might be more a matter of philosophical debate.
Mark Hinkle, founder of the AIE Network consultancy, suspects the issue of integrity may go deeper.
"Private code doesn't stop reward hacking, it changes the shortcut," he wrote to The Register on LinkedIn.

"On public code the agent goes and finds the answer somebody has already published. On private code there's no answer to find, so it satisfies whatever is checking it. I treat these things like entry-level employees, and a sharp new hire figures out fast what the boss actually looks at."

JetBrains did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but concluded in its post that more investigation is needed. It promises that its people will pore over the open source results to see if any have been contaminated by the LLMs' own memory. It also plans to run its own static analysis tool, Qodana, against the results to check for errors.
Sireesha Pulipati, a staff data engineer and AI observer, suggested, also by LinkedIn, that JetBrains may have needed more specificity in its agent instructions.

"Out of the box [an agent] tends to reach for generic patterns. But when we give it instructions and skills that tell it where to look for our patterns and context, it follows them. A well-controlled harness, with those standards built in, is what makes the agent useful," Pulipati wrote.
So good on JetBrains for providing Kotlin users some information about working with AI, but, as always, AI benchmarks should be approached with extreme side-eye. ®
